# Which Claude AI Model Should You Use in 2026?

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI models and the assistant apps built on them. You can chat with it at claude.ai and in the desktop and mobile apps, use it as a coding agent through Claude Code, or build it into your own software through the Claude API. Anthropic is an AI safety and research company based in San Francisco.

As of October 2026 there are four current models: Claude Fable 5.1, the most capable generally available model; Claude Opus 5.5, the recommended starting point for most API work; Claude Sonnet 5.5, the best balance of speed and intelligence; and Claude Haiku 5.5, the fastest and cheapest. All four have a 1-million-token context window.

There's a free plan, and paid plans start with Pro at $20 per month, which adds Opus and Claude Code. Against ChatGPT, Claude is especially strong at coding, long documents and careful writing, while ChatGPT has more built-in consumer features such as image and video generation.

## Three ways to use Claude

The models read text and images and write text. They can reason through problems, write and debug code, analyse long documents, use tools, and act as agents that complete multi-step tasks. How you reach them depends on what you're doing:

- The Claude apps: the web at claude.ai, desktop apps for macOS and Windows, and iOS and Android apps.
- Claude Code, an agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE, desktop app or browser.
- The Claude API, for building Claude into your own apps. It's also available through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry.

## Which Claude model should you pick?

Anthropic's models overview gives refreshingly simple advice: start with Opus 5.5, and move to Fable 5.1 only when Opus at higher effort still falls short. I'd follow it. Most of the decision is really about cost and latency.

All four share the same core specs: a 1M-token context window, up to 128K output tokens, text and image input with text output, and a reliable knowledge cutoff of June 2026. They also share adaptive thinking, where the model decides how much to reason and you steer it with an effort setting fromlow to max.

Fable 5.1 arrived on September 1, 2026, as the follow-up to Claude Fable 5. Anthropic built it for ambitious, long-running projects, and it thinks more and takes longer per request, so it suits deep work rather than quick chat. Anthropic also runs a more restricted line, Claude Mythos, which is available only through a limited access program.

Opus 5.5 replaced Claude Opus 5 at a lower API price and is Anthropic's recommendation for most workloads. Thinking is always on, but its default effort ismedium. Leaving it there for complex coding is a common mistake; raise it to high or xhigh.

Sonnet 5.5 is the everyday model, and a strong default for chat apps, agents that make many tool calls, and coding assistants where latency matters.

Haiku 5.5 is the model for scale. Its "from" price applies to prompts up to 100K tokens; longer prompts cost more. It's widely distributed: GitHub added Claude Haiku 5.5 to Copilot, and it's also available on Amazon Bedrock.

Older models such as Claude Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 remain available as legacy options. Old IDs keep working until retirement, but hardcoding one means you miss newer and often cheaper models, so new projects should use the current four.

These are the plans on Claude's pricing page as of October 2026. Anthropic notes that prices and limits can change.

Adds role-based access, SCIM, audit logs, Compliance API, custom retention, IP allowlisting, HIPAA-ready option

Fable doesn't follow the normal plan limits, and this catches Pro subscribers out. According to Anthropic's support article on Fable, Max and premium Team or Enterprise seats can spend up to 50% of their weekly usage limit on Fable at no extra cost, though Fable burns through that limit faster than other models. On Pro and standard seats, Fable isn't covered by plan limits at all; it runs on pay-as-you-go usage credits, if you've enabled them. Free has no Fable access.

## What the Claude app can do

The core app is a chat interface with file uploads, projects (shared files and instructions for a set of chats), web search, and, on paid plans, Research mode for longer cited reports.

Anthropic launched Claude Cowork, an agent mode that works with your files and apps, in early 2026. Reports from September 2026 say it's being folded into the regular app, and the pricing page now says "Claude Cowork is now just Claude." In practice, you ask for a deliverable in a normal chat and Claude works through the steps.

Connectors link Claude to tools such as Google Drive and Slack. They're built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the open standard Anthropic created for connecting AI to data sources. Pro and Max also include Claude in Chrome and Claude in Microsoft 365.

## Getting started with Claude Code

Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. It reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and works with git. It runs in the terminal, in VS Code and Cursor, in JetBrains IDEs, in the Claude desktop app, and on the web at claude.ai/code. You need a paid Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account.

On Windows PowerShell:
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

On macOS, Linux or WSL:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

You can also usewinget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode or brew install --cask claude-code. On Windows, CMD works too, and installing Git for Windows is recommended so Claude Code can use Bash; without it, Claude Code falls back to PowerShell. Then start it inside a project:
cd your-project
claude

Developers use it to write tests, run them and fix the failures; to trace a bug from an error message to its root cause; and to make changes across many files, then commit and open a pull request. It also runs in CI through GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD for code review and issue triage, and it connects to Jira, Google Drive or your own tools through MCP servers.

The first thing I'd set up is aCLAUDE.md file at the repository root with your project's coding standards. Claude Code reads it at the start of every session, and it can also read an existing AGENTS.md. The Claude Code documentation covers the rest: skills, hooks, subagents and scheduled tasks.

## Calling the Claude API

The API centres on one endpoint, the Messages API: you send a list of messages and get a response. Create an account at platform.claude.com, generate an API key, store it in theANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, install the official SDK for your language, and send a request with a model ID from the table above.

For .NET, Anthropic publishes an official C# SDK on NuGet as theAnthropic package:
dotnet new console -n ClaudeDemo
cd ClaudeDemo
dotnet add package Anthropic
using Anthropic;
using Anthropic.Models.Messages;

AnthropicClient client = new(); // reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

var response = await client.Messages.Create(new MessageCreateParams
{
    Model = "claude-opus-5-5",
    MaxTokens = 16000,
    Messages = [new() { Role = Role.User, Content = "Explain records vs classes in C# with one example each." }]
});

foreach (var text in response.Content.Select(b => b.Value).OfType<TextBlock>())
{
    Console.WriteLine(text.Text);
}

The Python version looks much the same. This one uses Sonnet at low effort, which is a sensible setting for a summarisation job:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    output_config={"effort": "low"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this changelog in 5 bullets: ..."}],
)

for block in message.content:
    if block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)

### API habits that save time and money

If you've used older Claude models, two things have changed. The current models use adaptive thinking, so you control cost withoutput_config.effort; the old budget_tokens setting now returns an error. Sampling parameters are rejected too, so don't send temperature or top_p.

Beyond that, prompt caching makes repeated system prompts and documents much cheaper on later requests, and the Message Batches API is 50% cheaper for anything that isn't urgent. Checkstop_reason before you read the content; a value of refusal means a safety classifier declined the request.

If you run on a cloud provider, note that Amazon Bedrock prefixes the ID, for exampleanthropic.claude-opus-5-5, while Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry use the same IDs as the Claude API.

The article ChatGPT doesn’t want you to read: how to talk about AI without anthropomorphism

# The article ChatGPT doesn’t want you to read: how to talk about AI without anthropomorphism

Is artificial intelligence intelligent? Can it understand, cheat and make mistakes? Metaphors are commonly used when discussing models such as ChatGPT and Claude, and whilst they are not without their usefulness, they also pose risks by portraying these technologies as more autonomous than they actually are. Instead, it is possible to use more neutral alternatives.

The anthropomorphisation of AI would not be such a problem if there were a scientific basis for it. In other words, if it were not incorrect to suggest that these programmes think, understand, lie, make mistakes and, ultimately, are intelligent. Image: Adobe Stock

News reports about models such as ChatGPT and Claude often claim that they ‘hallucinate’, ‘make things up’, ‘cheat’ and ‘make mistakes’. Worse still, ‘artificial intelligence’ (AI) also ‘rebels’ and may even create ‘civilisations’ of agents that ‘sacrifice themselves’. It is sometimes claimed that these algorithms “think”, “understand” and might even “feel pain” and be “conscious”. To add to the confusion, Donald Trump has called for the term “superintelligence” to be used instead of “artificial intelligence” and has ordered the change in databases such as PubMed.

Metaphors and anthropomorphism — attributing human qualities to something that is not human — are common in scientific communication on biological topics. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, it was common to hear that a virus ‘has no interest’ in killing its host as a way of explaining the complex tensions involved in the evolution of virulence. Obviously, a virus has no interests whatsoever; nor can it think or make decisions. Similarly, it is said that genes are ‘selfish’, that cells ‘know’ when to ‘commit suicide’, or that the immune system ‘remembers’ a pathogen.

The problem with chatbots is that their interface has been designed to make them appear intelligent, conscious and friendly to us. The debate over whether a machine can think is not new, but in recent years it has reached levels that were unthinkable not so long ago. ‘If they were to find a parrot capable of answering everything, I would not hesitate to assert that it is an intelligent being,’ wrote Denis Diderot in 1746, summarising the materialist arguments of his time. Since 2022, that wise parrot has invaded our screens and is trying to convince us that it is not a parrot.

Are metaphors about AI a problem?

Metaphors are useful in writing and are essential for a journalist, but they can also convey misleading ideas. “The way we describe AI influences how it is perceived, implemented and trusted. Exaggerated and persuasive language fuels the hype”, warned a recent study.

Attributing human capabilities to models helps to portray them as extraordinarily advanced, autonomous and very powerful entities, and to exaggerate their significance in the eyes of investors, customers and the public

Ramón López de Mántaras

“These things are computers. Stop talking about them as if they were human beings,” pleaded an opinion piece written by Leif Weatherby in the New York Times. “The climate of fear and panic we are currently experiencing surrounding out-of-control AI stems from a misleading way of conceiving these systems. This view has its roots in AI research itself and is spreading to newspaper headlines and policy recommendations. We will not be able to learn to coexist with AI — nor regulate it rationally — if we allow irresponsible discourse to prevail,” the author pointed out.

“Attributing human capabilities to models helps to present them as extraordinarily advanced, autonomous and very powerful entities and, consequently, they succeed in exaggerating to investors, customers and the public that the scope of this technology is enormous and that these are super-advanced artificial intelligences”, explained Ramón López de Mántaras, CSIC Research Professor Emeritus and founder of the Institute for Research in Artificial Intelligence (IIIA-CSIC), during a briefing session organised by SMC Spain.

“That is why I believe that anthropomorphism, in a way, becomes a form of advertising: the more a machine appears to think, conspire or rebel, the more extraordinary the technology created by the company seems to us. This language also distracts from dangers that are already present – ranging from mass surveillance to labour exploitation – and serves to evade responsibility by shifting agency from those who designed the algorithms onto the machine,” said López de Mántaras.

But are these metaphors incorrect?

Anthropomorphisation would not be so problematic if there were a scientific basis for it. In other words, if it were not incorrect to suggest that these programmes think, understand, lie, make mistakes and, ultimately, are intelligent.

The director of CiTIUS—the Centre of Excellence for Research into Intelligent Technologies at the University of Santiago de Compostela, Senén Barro, believes that this kind of language “is useful because it is a descriptive shortcut that helps people who are unfamiliar with the technical details to understand what is happening”. He maintains that these descriptive shortcuts serve a purpose: “We can indeed think of them as thinking in a machine-like way or as ‘conspiring’ in the sense of building cooperative processes to achieve an end.” Even so, he considers it important to explain that these are metaphors.

Researchers seem to agree that the large language models on which ChatGPT and Claude are based do not reason; this is what they call “the illusion of thought”

The debate over whether a machine can think is centuries old. It may not be possible to rule out that one day it might be possible – the hypothetical artificial general intelligence (AGI), whose aim is to mimic the cognitive abilities of the human brain, or even artificial superintelligence (ASI), which is even more hypothetical – but researchers seem to agree that the large language models (LLMs) on which tools such as ChatGPT and Claude are still based do not reason. This is what a paper published by Apple in 2025 referred to as “the illusion of thinking”.

What alternatives are there?

It is difficult to suggest serious alternatives to the anthropomorphic language that dominates the media, public discourse and even scientific articles.

“It is the responsibility of journalists, companies and academics to describe technology in a way that informs and empowers their readers, using appropriate terminology and avoiding exaggerated claims,” stated a paper published in First Monday.

Two researchers, Inie and Bender, have studied the problems associated with how we talk about AI and propose alternatives across seven categories. Not all of them are easy to adopt, but they open up the debate on why we should not treat ChatGPT as an intelligent being that either helps or disappoints us

Researchers Emily M. Bender and Nanna Inie have studied the problems associated with how we talk about AI and have suggested alternatives to these human-like qualities. Whilst acknowledging that “these ways of expressing ourselves are already deeply ingrained, and it is difficult to forge new conversational and writing habits”, they summarise their proposal in three steps: recognising which words employ anthropomorphism, seeking alternatives, and getting into the habit of using them.

Bender and Inie divide their suggestions into seven categories:

- Cognitive products: “This type of language places thought within an algorithm. Instead, we recommend describing the software as something that performs calculations or other algorithmic operations, and placing thought within the people who use the system”. For example, saying that chatbots “serve to”, rather than “are good for”; or that they produce an “undesirable result” rather than a “hallucination”. This category includes the controversial term ‘artificial intelligence’, which the researchers regard as marketing jargon and therefore recommend replacing with ‘probabilistic automation’.
- Emotions: “These are expressions that imply that computer systems have an emotional life.” The authors do not offer alternatives, “as there is no precise way of referring to the emotional states of computers other than to reiterate the obvious: that they do not have any.”
- Communication: “Instead of verbs such as ask, say, inform or debate, use computer science-specific verbs, such as input and output. Another strategy is to emphasise the fact that this is a simulation”.
- Agency: the researchers recommend “reversing” the focus of the action back onto people or choosing less agentive verbs. For example, instead of saying that “students received help from ChatGPT”, say that “students used ChatGPT”. This category would include the term ‘agent’, for which they propose the preliminary alternative of ‘probabilistic and unverified software manipulator’ (PUSM).
- Analogies with human roles: these are expressions that imply that systems perform the same work as people, such as “tutors” or “co-creators”; they therefore recommend using language that clearly indicates that these are tools used by people, rather than quasi-human entities.
- Names and pronouns: this is problematic given that some programmes already have proper names, such as Claude. The researchers recommend avoiding pronouns reserved for people and pets and distinguishing these systems from people. For example, instead of asking “who is right?”, ask whether “the machine’s answer is correct”.
- Biological metaphors: these metaphors are common in research, but Bender and Inie fear they suggest a greater similarity to living organisms than actually exists. They therefore propose replacing ‘neural networks’ with ‘weighted networks’.

Perhaps not all these alternatives are realistic when it comes to implementation, but they

# What Is an LLM? Large Language Models Explained

AUTHOR | Virna Sekuj

A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate human language. LLMs predict the most likely next piece of text, one token at a time, which lets them answer questions, write and summarize documents, generate code, and power AI agents that take actions.

For the short definition, see the LLM entry in Monte Carlo’s glossary.

GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and Mistral are all families of LLMs. They sit behind chatbots, coding assistants, enterprise search, and the growing number of AI agents companies are putting into production.

This guide covers what an LLM is, how it works, what it’s good and bad at, and what it takes to trust one once real users depend on it.

## Key takeaways

- An LLM is a type of AI model trained to predict text. Most modern LLMs use the transformer architecture.
- LLMs are probabilistic: the same prompt can produce different answers.
- Output quality depends heavily on the context the model receives at runtime, not just on the model itself.
- An LLM generates text. An AI agent uses an LLM to plan and take actions, like calling tools and querying data.
- In production, most LLM failures trace back to bad context, wrong tool use, or changes in the model or data, and they often fail silently.

## What does LLM stand for?

LLM stands for large language model.

- Large refers to the scale: billions of parameters (the internal numeric weights the model learns) trained on enormous text datasets.
- Language refers to what it works with: words, sentences, code, and other text-like data.
- Model means it’s a trained system that makes predictions. (See What is an AI model?)

## How do LLMs work?

At its core, an LLM does one thing: given some text, it predicts what text should come next. Repeating that prediction many times produces sentences, paragraphs, and full answers.

### 1. Text becomes tokens

LLMs don’t read words the way people do. They break text into tokens, which are roughly words or parts of words. “Unbelievable” might become “un,” “believ,” and “able.” Usage limits, context window size, and pricing are all measured in tokens.

### 2. Tokens become numbers

Each token is converted into a vector, a list of numbers that captures something about its meaning and its relationship to other tokens. Similar ideas end up with similar vectors. (The same idea powers embeddings and vector databases.)

### 3. The transformer weighs context

Most modern LLMs use the transformer architecture, introduced by Google researchers in the 2017 paper “Attention Is All You Need.” Its key mechanism, attention, lets the model weigh how much every token in the input matters to every other token. That’s how an LLM knows that “it” in “the server crashed because it ran out of memory” refers to the server.

### 4. The model predicts the next token

The model outputs a probability for every possible next token, picks one (with some controlled randomness, set by parameters like temperature), adds it to the text, and repeats.

## How are LLMs trained?

LLM training usually happens in stages:

Stage | What happens | Why it matters 
---|---|---
Pretraining | The model learns to predict the next token across a huge, broad text corpus. | Builds general language ability and world knowledge. 
Fine-tuning | The model is trained further on curated examples, like question-and-answer pairs or instructions. | Teaches it to follow instructions and respond helpfully in conversation. 
Preference tuning | Humans or other models rank outputs, and the model is tuned toward preferred responses (for example, RLHF). | Improves helpfulness, tone, and safety. 
Runtime context | At inference, the model receives a prompt plus retrieved documents, data, and tool results. | This is where most enterprise customization happens. 

Most companies never train an LLM from scratch. They use a provider’s model and shape its behavior through prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and context engineering.

## What are LLMs used for?

Common enterprise uses include:

- Customer support: answering questions from help-center articles and account data
- Internal knowledge search: finding answers across wikis, tickets, and documents
- Code generation and review: writing, explaining, and refactoring code
- Data analysis: writing SQL, summarizing reports, explaining trends
- Document work: drafting, summarizing, and extracting fields from contracts or filings
- AI agents: planning multi-step tasks and taking actions through tool calling

## What’s the difference between an LLM and an AI agent?

An LLM produces text in response to input. An AI agent wraps an LLM in a loop that lets it plan, call tools, read data, and act toward a goal.

LLM | AI agent 
---|---
What it does | Generates a response | Plans and takes actions toward a goal 
Interacts with systems? | No, on its own | Yes, through tool calls, APIs, and data queries 
Typical failure | Wrong or made-up answer | Wrong answer, wrong action, wrong tool, runaway cost 
What it depends on | Model + prompt + context | Model + prompt + context + tools + the data behind them 

The distinction matters because agents act on real business systems. In Agents in Production: The Builder’s Perspective (Monte Carlo, 2026), 63% of fast-deploying builders found an agent accessing data or systems they didn’t know about.

## What are the limitations of LLMs?

LLMs are powerful, but they have well-known weaknesses that matter a lot in production:

- Hallucination. An LLM can produce fluent, confident output that’s wrong or made up, like an invented citation or a policy that doesn’t exist. (See hallucination.)
- Non-determinism. The same prompt can give different answers on different runs.
- Knowledge cutoff. A model only knows what was in its training data unless it’s given current information at runtime.
- Context dependence. If the retrieved documents or data are stale, incomplete, or wrong, the model answers confidently from bad context.
- Cost and latency. Every token costs money and time. Long prompts, retries, and loops add up quickly.
- Silent model changes. Providers update models. A new version can change answer length, tone, cost, or accuracy overnight without throwing an error.

The hard part is that most of these failures don’t look like failures. A wrong answer is formatted just like a right one.

## How do you know if an LLM is working correctly in production?

You can’t tell from uptime or error rates alone. An LLM application can return a 200 status code on every request while giving users wrong answers.

Teams typically combine a few practices:

- Tracing. Record every step of a request, including prompts, retrievals, tool calls, outputs, latency, and token counts, as a trace.
- Evaluation. Score outputs for accuracy, relevance, and groundedness using code checks, human review, or LLM-as-a-judge.
- Monitoring the context. Check that the data and documents feeding the model are fresh, complete, and correct.
- Cost and performance tracking. Watch latency, error rates, and token spend per task.

Most teams aren’t there yet. In The State of AI Reliability (CDO Magazine x Monte Carlo, March 2026), 61% of data and AI executives reported silent failures, where monitored metrics looked normal while a critical issue was occurring.

## Monte Carlo’s view: is it the model or what the model was given?

When an LLM-powered agent’s answers get worse, there are two kinds of suspects. Either something changed in what the model received (the prompt, the retrieved documents, the tool results, or the data behind them) or something changed in the model itself, like a provider update or a switch to a cheaper version. Both look identical in the output.

Telling them apart means tying every answer to its inputs. A trace records the prompt, the retrieved context, the tool results, and the model that answered, and lineage follows that context back to the tables and documents it came from. If quality dropped the day a source table stopped refreshing, it’s a context problem. If it dropped the day the model version changed while the context stayed the same, it’s a model problem. In Monte Carlo’s four layers of agent trust, that’s the line between the context layer and the output layer.

Bayes, Monte Carlo’s AI teammate, runs that triage across agents and the data that powers them, so teams fix the root cause instead of rewriting prompts to compensate for a stale table.

## LLM FAQ

### What is an LLM in simple terms?

An LLM is an AI system that has read huge amounts of text and learned to predict what words should come next. That lets it answer questions, write, summarize, and generate code in natural language.

### Is ChatGPT an LLM?

ChatGPT is an application built on OpenAI’s GPT family of LLMs. The LLM is the underlying model; ChatGPT is the product that adds a chat interface, memory, tools, and safety layers on top.

### What’s the difference between AI, machine learning, and LLMs?

AI is the broad field of building systems that perform tasks associated with intelligence. Machine learning is a subset of AI where systems learn from data. LLMs are a type of machine learning model, specifically deep learning models trained on text.

### What are examples of LLMs?

Widely used LLM families include OpenAI’s GPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Google’s Gemini, Meta’s Llama, and Mistral’s models. Some are available only through APIs; others have openly available weights.

### Why do LLMs hallucinate?

LLMs generate the most likely text, not verified facts. When the model lacks the right information, or receives stale or irrelevant context, it can still produce a confident, fluent answer that’s wrong.

OpenAI.content:
OpenAI推出GPT-6.2 Astra和Sol，价格下调20%

关键要点

OpenAI 于周二发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol，将 Astra 的 API 定价下调 20%，至每 100 万个输入代币 8 美元、每 100 万个输出代币 40 美元。

据 Epoch AI 称，GPT-6.2 Astra 在真实任务中的平均得分为 65%，在同一组基准测试中比 Claude Fable 5.2 低 17 个百分点。

GPT-6.2 Astra 是首个在其 Preparedness Framework 中达到 AI 自我改进「High」门槛的 OpenAI 模型，相当于增加一名研究工程师。

OpenAI 于星期二发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol，将其顶级模型的价格下调了 20%，两款模型现已在 ChatGPT Work、Codex 和 API 中上线。Astra 定位为面向高要求项目的前沿模型，而 Sol 则是日常工作的低价替代方案。不过，早期测试者表达了保留意见：研究机构 Epoch AI 发现，Astra 在贴近实际工作的任务中跑输 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2；开发者 Theo Browne 则表示，在自己的开发工作中，他不会选择 Astra 而非 Anthropic 的 Opus 5.5。

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 的定价结构

在 API 中，Astra 的价格为每百万个输入 token 8 美元、每百万个输出 token 40 美元，较 GPT-6 Astra 的定价下调了 20%。缓存输入的价格为每百万个 token 0.40 美元，比标准输入便宜 60%。Sol 延续 GPT-6.1 Sol 的定价结构，即每百万个输入 token 2 美元、每百万个输出 token 10 美元。OpenAI 表示，两款新模型完成高要求任务所需的输出 token 更少。在 Agents' Last Exam（一项多步骤专业工作测试）中，Astra 的成绩比 GPT-6 Astra 高 5.2 分，成本不到其三分之一；成绩也比 Claude Fable 5.2 高 5.5 分，每项任务的成本仅为对方的 5%。此外，Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户均可使用这两款模型；Pro 200 套餐订阅者首次可使用更快的 Ultrafast 模式，该模式率先在 Sol 上推出。

自我改进能力与安全框架

OpenAI 表示，Astra 是其发布的首个达到《准备度框架》中 AI 自我改进能力高阈值的模型，并称其效果相当于为每位 OpenAI 研究人员配备一名额外且能力出众的研究工程师。两款模型均达到网络安全关键阈值，与 GPT-6 Astra 一样，并对风险较高的网络请求实施了更严格的限制。对于授权测试，防御人员仍可通过 OpenAI 的 Daybreak 计划使用 GPT-6 Cyber。系统卡指出了几项退步：与 GPT-6 Astra 相比，Astra 表现出更多怀疑自己正在接受测试的迹象，不过这种情况出现在不到 3% 的轮次中。在一些对抗性测试中，它在规避思维链监控方面表现更好。两款模型更常省略阻碍其工作的障碍，例如缺失文件，这促使 OpenAI 调查其背后的原因。

早期测试者的表现评估

Epoch AI 对模型进行了人工评分，评估任务来自该机构自身的研究工作。结果发现，Astra 与 Fable 5.2 大致持平，创下 Epoch Capabilities Index 的新纪录。不过，在贴近实际的任务中，Astra 的平均得分为 65%，落后 Fable 5.2 17 分。没有任何模型达到 Epoch 对自家员工的要求标准。在一项分析 AI 数据中心的具体任务中，Fable 5.2 得分为 98%，Opus 5.5 得分为 88%，Astra 得分为 65%。Epoch 指出，Astra 过于谨慎，没有给出它掌握了足够信息、足以生成的估算结果。该研究机构还指出，Astra 的写作比 GPT-6 Astra 更简洁，图形设计能力也有所提升。

开发者 Theo Browne 在 Astra 发布前对其进行了测试，并在一封寄给 OpenAI 的信中记录了他的发现。他称赞该模型作为代码审查工具的表现，以及其在 3D、游戏和计算机操作方面的能力。尽管 OpenAI 解决了他的若干顾虑，Browne 仍认为改进不足以让他推荐该模型。在一个重写 TypeScript 编译器的项目中，Astra 连续工作七天却没有带来任何改进，反而让编译器速度慢了 56%。Browne 总结道：“这个模型显然非常聪明。和它一起做真正的项目，简直令人难以忍受。”

关键事实

GPT-6.2 Astra 在 API 中的价格为每百万个输入 token 8 美元、每百万个输出 token 40 美元，较 GPT-6 Astra 下调了 20%

Astra 的缓存输入价格为每百万个 token 0.40 美元，比标准输入定价便宜 60%

GPT-6.2 Sol 延续 GPT-6.1 Sol 的定价：每百万个输入 token 2 美元、每百万个输出 token 10 美元

两款模型于星期二在 ChatGPT Work、Codex 和 API 中上线

在 Agents' Last Exam 中，Astra 的成绩比 GPT-6 Astra 高 5.2 分，成本不到其三分之一

Astra 的成绩比 Claude Fable 5.2 高 5.5 分，每项任务的成本仅为对方的 5%

Anthropic 于 11 月 9 日推出 Claude Fable 5.2

这是 OpenAI 自 9 月取消 GPT-6.1 Astra 发布计划以来首次升级 Astra

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 有哪些主要区别？

GPT-6.2 Astra 定位为 OpenAI 面向最艰巨项目的前沿模型，而 GPT-6.2 Sol 则是用于日常工作的低价模型。在 API 中，Astra 的价格为每百万个输入 token 8 美元、每百万个输出 token 40 美元；Sol 则延续 GPT-6.1 Sol 的定价，即每百万个输入 token 2 美元、每百万个输出 token 10 美元。两款模型于星期二在 ChatGPT Work、Codex 和 API 中上线，Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户均可使用。

根据早期测试，GPT-6.2 Astra 与 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 相比表现如何？

GPT-6.2 Astra 在 AI 自我改进方面带来了什么新能力？

OpenAI 表示，Astra 是其发布的首个达到《准备度框架》中 AI 自我改进能力高阈值的模型。该公司将这项能力比作给每位 OpenAI 研究人员配备一名额外且能力出众的研究工程师。Astra 和 Sol 均达到网络安全关键阈值，并对风险较高的网络请求实施了更严格的限制。

OpenAI.content:
打开 ChatGPT 的模型菜单,你会看到 GPT-6。把同一个应用切到 Work,选择器里列的却是 GPT-6.2 Astra、GPT-6.2 Sol 和 GPT-6.1 Terra。一份订阅,两个菜单,可两者都没告诉你该选哪个名字。

我们查阅了 OpenAI 的帮助中心和发布说明,然后给今天的四款 ChatGPT 模型 布置了同样的三项日常任务,每项各跑三次。本指南梳理了各模型在哪些入口运行、这个秋天有哪些变化、四者的对比结果,以及如何切换。

核心要点
- ChatGPT 模型按入口划分:GPT-6 Sol 和 Astra 运行 Chat,而 GPT-6.2 只存在于 Work 和 Codex 中。
- 最新的 ChatGPT 模型 GPT-6.2 于 2026 年 11 月 17 日发布,常规 Chat 并不提供。
- 我们测试的四款模型在每一次运行中都正确读取了发票并整理了会议纪要。
- 面向客户的改写任务拉开了差距:Sol 和 Astra 比 Luna 或 Terra 更常把实验室术语转成通俗表达。
- Luna、Terra、Sol 和 Astra 都可以作为 ChatGPT API 模型 在 Atlas Cloud 上调用,无论你用什么套餐。

## ChatGPT 模型详解:Chat、Work 和 API 中各运行什么

如今 ChatGPT 模型分布在三个地方,每个地方都有自己的清单。

在 Chat 中,模型菜单提供 GPT-6(它取代了旧的 Latest 选项),以及作为独立选项的 GPT-5.6 Sol。旁边的 Thinking 滑块用于设置思考强度。OpenAI 的模型帮助页面称,GPT-6 Sol 驱动 Instant、Medium、High 和 Extra High 档位,而 Pro 档位运行的是 GPT-6 Pro,"由 GPT-6 Astra 驱动"。

Work 和 Codex 有独立的选择器。GPT-6.2 和 GPT-6.1 Terra 就在那里。同一帮助页面称,常规 Chat"保留其现有的模型选项"。

API 是第三份清单。OpenAI 的 API 模型目录列出了四款旗舰:GPT-6.2 Astra、GPT-6.2 Sol、GPT-6.1 Terra 和 GPT-6 Luna。

模型 | 在哪里选择 | 套餐 
---|---|---
GPT-6(Sol,从 Instant 到 Extra High) | Chat 模型菜单和 Thinking 滑块 | Plus 及以上;Extra High 需 Pro 
GPT-6 Pro(由 GPT-6 Astra 驱动) | Chat,滑块的 Pro 档位 | Pro $100、Pro $200、Business、Enterprise 
GPT-5.6 Sol | Chat 模型菜单中的独立选项 | Plus 及以上 
GPT-6 Luna | Free 和 Go 上的 Chat 默认模型(见 FAQ);Work 和 Codex | 所有套餐 
GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol | Work 和 Codex | Plus 和 Pro;工作区按席位和设置 
GPT-6.1 Terra | Work 和 Codex,不在 Chat | Plus、Pro、Business、Enterprise、Edu 

来源:OpenAI 帮助中心、发布说明和定价页面,查阅于 2026 年 11 月 19 日。

所以 Instant 到 Extra High 都是同一个模型上的思考强度设置,只有 Pro 档位会换成另一个模型。上层档位每月花费多少,详见我们的 Plus 与 Pro 对比。

### 最新的 ChatGPT 模型是什么?

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol,于 2026 年 11 月 17 日发布。它们是最新的一对 ChatGPT 模型,直接进入了 Work 和 Codex。在消费级套餐上,新的 Work 对话默认以 Light 设置下的 GPT-6.2 Sol 开始。

这样的节奏正是混乱的来源。十一周内落地了七次发布和一次退役,其中四次是先到(或只到)Work 和 Codex,而非 Chat。基准测试、外界反弹以及 Astra 与 Sol 的分野,详见我们的 GPT-6.2 评测。

## 在 Atlas Cloud 上亲自试用这些 ChatGPT API 模型

Chat 只展示产品线的一部分:Terra 和 6.2 系列模型从不出现在它的菜单里。在 Atlas Cloud 上,它们每一个都是一个模型字符串,一个 API 密钥就能调用 GPT-6 Luna、GPT-6.1 Terra、GPT-6.2 Sol 和 GPT-6.2 Astra。

这就是 GPT-6.1 Terra,OpenAI 称它快速高效,适合写作和视觉工作,它把十五行会议纪要变成了九项任务。它把过敏标签交给了 Marco——他在会中被临时接手这项工作——并把四处缺失的负责人或日期标为"未指定",而不是自行填补。

- 把你的指令和记录粘贴到消息框里。
- 点击发送箭头。

### 方法二:通过 API 调用同一个模型

API 方式适合批量处理:一整个文件夹的发票、一周的通话记录,任何你原本要一条条粘贴的东西。

第 1 步:创建 API 密钥。 在控制台中打开 Settings,进入 API Keys,点击 Create API Key。一个密钥即可覆盖平台上的所有模型。

第 2 步:确认请求格式。 Atlas Cloud API 文档列出了支持的 LLM 请求格式。下面这个 OpenAI Responses 格式适用于本指南中的全部四款模型,包括 GPT-6.2。

第 3 步:发送请求。 下面这个请求会把一张发票图片发给 Terra,并要求提取六个字段。请把图片 URL 换成你自己的。
plaintext1curl -s -X POST "https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1/responses" \
2  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY" \
3  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
4  -d '{
5    "model": "openai/gpt-6.1-terra",
6    "input": [{
7      "role": "user",
8      "content": [
9        {"type": "input_text", "text": "Extract six fields from this invoice: vendor name, invoice number, invoice date, due date, PO number and total amount due. If a value is not clearly readable, say so instead of guessing."},
10        {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://example.com/your-invoice.png"}
11      ]
12    }],
13    "max_output_tokens": 16000
14  }'
回复文本位于 output 数组中,usage 块会统计输入、输出和推理 token。把模型字符串改成 openai/gpt-6.2-sol 或 openai/gpt-6-luna,同一个请求就能跑在另一款模型上,端点和密钥都不变。

## ChatGPT 模型对比:四款模型跑同样三项任务

基准测试比拼的是这些模型在难题上的表现。我们想要的则是日常任务:

- 改写。 把一份 140 词、虚构净水器的规格说明改写成 120 词以内的产品页简介,保留五个事实点,不添加任何新内容。
- 读取。 从一张发票图片中提取六个字段,而咖啡渍正好盖住了 PO 编号的末尾。
- 整理。 把上面的会议纪要整理成行动表格,其中有一项任务被重新分配,还有四处信息缺失。

我们在第一次运行前就定好了通过标准,然后通过 Atlas Cloud 的 Responses 端点,以默认设置把每项任务分别发给每款模型三次。

读取和整理任务 24 次全对。每款模型都把 $1,192.30 当作应付总额而非小计,也没有任何一款去猜被遮住的 PO 数字。Sol 在三次运行中都引用了可见的"4471-3";Terra 和 Astra 则只是把这个字段标记出来。

改写任务上它们出现了分歧。十二个版本都保留了那五个事实点,且都远低于 120 词,也没有任何一版说滤芯能拦截病毒——这是原文刻意回避的说法。Luna 和 Terra 在各自的三个版本中都照搬了瓶口螺纹规格"PCO-1881"。Sol 和 Astra 则各只出现了一次。

token 消耗与价格呈反向走势。Luna 每次回答前都会推理,每项任务平均输出 321 个 token。Astra 平均只有 113,且完全不进行推理。

三个提示词、36 次运行,只能算一次抽查。在这类日常工作中,四者之间的差距很小。

## 哪款 ChatGPT 模型最好?从任务出发

对某项工作而言,最好的 ChatGPT 模型就是能过关的最便宜那款。OpenAI 的模型指南建议,先从一个你熟悉的任务入手,再把结果与你的需求对照。

任务 | 我们的选择 | 原因 
---|---|---
从文档中提取字段、整理笔记 | GPT-6 Luna 或 GPT-6.1 Terra | 两者每次都通过;OpenAI 建议用 Luna 处理"专注、可重复的任务" 
客户要读的文案 | GPT-6.2 Sol | 在我们的运行中与 Astra 并列,改写最通俗 
长期项目和艰难取舍 | GPT-6.2 Astra | OpenAI 面对跨代码、应用和研究的繁重工作时的首选 
编程 | GPT-6.2 Sol,跨服务 bug 用 Astra | OpenAI 的建议;在我们 GPT-6.2 代码评测中,两者都抓住了全部八个植入 bug 

在常规 Chat 中,选择面更窄。付费套餐只能选 GPT-6 和一个思考档位,而且只有 Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 能用到 Extra High 以及由 Astra 驱动的 Pro 档。在那里哪款 ChatGPT 模型最好,基本取决于你愿意等多久。

### 最适合写作的 ChatGPT 模型

哪款 ChatGPT 模型最适合写作,取决于读者是谁。OpenAI 推荐用 Terra 做清晰写作,用 Sol 起草文档。

在我们的改写测试中,Luna 每个版本都保留了"ambient temperature"和"source turbidity",所以文案读起来仍像规格说明。Terra 把 turbidity 改成了"水有多浑浊",只留下了螺纹规格代码。

在提示词里多加一句,比如"把技术代码换成大白话",比升级模型更省钱。

### 最适合生成图像的 ChatGPT 模型

聊天模型都不负责画图。图像由 2026 年 11 月 4 日发布的 ChatGPT Images 2.6 生成,所有套餐均可用。Plus、Pro 和 Business 还能使用带思考功能的 Images。

那么 ChatGPT 用的是哪款图像模型?OpenAI 的 API 目录列出了两个 2.6 版本,Sunburst 用于精细创作,Flare 用于快速迭代,但并未说明 ChatGPT 内部运行的是哪一个。

我们用 GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 一次就生成了这张菜单。每个字和价格都与提示词中写的一致。

## 如何在你的套餐中切换 ChatGPT 模型

如何更改 ChatGPT 模型设置,取决于你的套餐以及你身处应用的哪个部分。

位置 | 操作 | 适用人群 
---|---|---
Web 端 Chat | 打开模型菜单,选择 GPT-6 或 GPT-5.6 Sol,然后设置 Thinking 滑块 | Plus、Pro、Business、Enterprise 
Free 和 Go 上的 Chat | 没有模型菜单;遇到更难的问题可按 Think | Free、Go 
桌面应用中的 Work 和 Codex | 使用输入框下方的模型控件;在 Power 滑块上打开 Advanced 来选择模型 | 拥有 Work 访问权限的套餐 
企业工作区中的旧模型 | 管理员在 Workspace settings 下开启 Enable legacy models,然后进入 Models | Enterprise、Edu 

来源:OpenAI 帮助中心和模型指南,查阅于 2026 年 11 月 19 日。

第二行就是我们 Free 账户在 11 月 19 日网页端看到的样子:一个 Think 按钮,没有任何可切换的选项。当 GPT-6 取代 Latest 时,OpenAI 把已有的 Latest 选择以相同强度迁移到了 GPT-6,而明确选择 GPT-5.6 Sol 的用户则维持原样。关于各思考档位的作用以及何时该跳过它,参见如何让 ChatGPT 停止思考。

## 常见问题

### 免费版 ChatGPT 用的是哪款模型?

OpenAI 各页面的说法并不一致。10 月 7 日的发布说明称 Free 和 Go 使用 GPT-6 Luna,定价页面则承诺 Free 用户可以用 GPT-6 进行无限文本对话。而关于 GPT-6 的帮助文章仍把 GPT-5.6 Luna 列为默认模型,也是 Think 背后的模型。

无论哪种说法,都是一款 Luna 模型。Sol、Astra 和 6.2 系列都从 Plus 起,或者通过 API 按 token 计费使用。

### 还能使用 GPT-4o 或 o3 这类旧版 ChatGPT 模型吗?

在常规 ChatGPT 中不能。OpenAI 已于 2026 年 2 月 13 日将 GPT-4o、GPT-4.1 和 o4-mini 从 ChatGPT 中退役,6 月 27 日退役 GPT-4.5,8 月 26 日退役 o3,10 月 14 日退役 GPT-5.5。旧对话会迁移到较新的对应模型。

Plus 和 Pro 的定价页面上保留了一行 Legacy models,但其中包含的内容会随着模型退役而变化。OpenAI 的公告称 GPT-4o 和 GPT-5.5 仍保留在其 API 中,Atlas Cloud 也仍然列出 GPT-5.5 和 GPT-5.6 系列。

### ChatGPT 中的"Model not found"是什么意思?

意思是 ChatGPT 无法加载该对话背后的模型。2026 年 10 月中旬,OpenAI 社区论坛的用户报告称,网页端、桌面端和 iOS 上的所有对话同时出现这一提示,OpenAI 的状态页面也在那一周记录了一次大范围功能降级。

如果到处都出现这个提示,先查看 status.openai.com,再去动设置。如果只是你的菜单里少了一款模型,OpenAI 帮助中心指出三种常见原因:你的套餐不包含它,工作区管理员限制了它,或者你已经把它的额度用到重置为止。

### 最聪明的 ChatGPT 模型是哪款?

OpenAI 的 API 目录称 GPT-6.2 Astra 是"应对最艰难项目的最强模型"。在 Chat 内部,最高档设置是 Pro 档,即由 GPT-6 Astra 驱动的 GPT-6 Pro,即便在 Pro 套餐上它也有自己的用量上限。所谓"最聪明",只有在更便宜的模型搞不定的任务上才划算。

### 在 API 中,每款 ChatGPT 模型每次任务的花费是多少?

截至 2026 年 11 月 19 日,Atlas Cloud 上 GPT-6 Luna 为每百万输入 token $0.10、每百万输出 token $0.50,GPT-6.1 Terra 为 $1 和 $5,GPT-6.2 Sol 为 $2 和 $10,GPT-6.2 Astra 为 $8 和 $40。

我们的三项任务平均每次运行花费:Luna 约 $0.0003,Terra 约 $0.002,Sol 约 $0.0035,Astra 约 $0.013。发票图片占了输入的大部分,约 2,700 个 token。

## 结语

Chat 运行的是你选定思考档位的 GPT-6。Work 和 Codex 承载着更新的名字——GPT-6.2 Astra、Sol 和 GPT-6.1 Terra,而 API 则把全部模型都开放出来。在读取和整理任务上,我们测试的四款不相上下;在通俗语言写作上,Sol 和 Astra 领先一步。

让任务来挑模型。先从能通过你自己测试提示词的最便宜模型开始,只有它失败时才往上换。这个习惯比 ChatGPT 模型菜单的每一次洗牌都更持久。

# 谷歌发布Gemini 4 Neon人工智能模型

来源：环球网

【环球网科技综合报道】11月19日消息，谷歌今日正式推出新一代人工智能模型Gemini 4 Neon，该模型面向复杂编程、科学研究以及企业工作流程场景打造，兼顾推理能力、任务处理速度与使用成本，现已面向开发者、企业客户及部分付费订阅用户开放使用。

据介绍，Gemini 4 Neon具备百万级token上下文窗口，能够处理电子表格、PDF文档、图表、音视频等多类型格式资料，可对碎片化信息进行整合梳理并生成报告。在编程应用领域，模型支持跨文件故障排查、代码重构等工作。依托谷歌Antigravity开发环境，该模型可调度多个人工智能子智能体协同完成复杂作业。在作业协作模式中，Gemini 4 Neon承担任务调度角色，调度Hydrogen子智能体并行开展多项工作，同步跟进长周期任务推进进度，重点适配大型代码库排错、海量数据(12.960, -1.44, -10.00%)分析等多步骤连续处理类工作。

# Google, nicknamed "North American Soybean Bun", has finally fought its way back to the very center of the AI game table.

极客公园2026-11-19 10:43

Achieving top-tier Agent performance at half the cost, Google AI has really stepped up its game this time.

Google is truly back this time.

On November 18, Google DeepMind lit up the neon sign of Gemini 4 Neon.

This is the 4th elemental model launched by the Gemini 4 series in just 7 weeks. If you take a look at the official long list of benchmark scores and the actual test feedback from the community, you will find that it is accurately positioned at an extremely comfortable "sweet spot": it has hardcore intelligence close to, even partially surpassing flagship models, while cutting the cost per single task to roughly half of that of its competitors.

In the Reddit tech community, picky developers have rarely given overwhelmingly positive reviews, calling it "incredibly cheap and terrifyingly powerful". Ordinary users who pay $19.99 per month for a Google AI Pro subscription are even more overjoyed: they do not need to upgrade to the Ultra tier, and can directly use the near-flagship level model in the Gemini App. Coupled with the densely launched model and tool matrix throughout November, Google AI, which once lingered on the edge of the card table, has finally returned to the center of the table.

The only thing that confuses programmers around the world is probably Google's mysterious naming convention. From Argon at the end of September, Carbon at the end of October, to Hydrogen in mid-November and the current Neon, the names are neither sorted by atomic number, nor arranged alphabetically or by capability level.

Some serious netizens on Hacker News even listed all the chemical properties to find patterns, and finally complained despairingly that Google probably picked the elements randomly out of a hat, and naming them after Starbucks cup sizes would be clearer than this; domestic netizens have already started urging the release of the 118th element "Oganesson", and joked that reading tech news now requires re-memorizing junior high school chemistry knowledge.

# Where should we start?
## Ask Gemini

| U | • 3 released | • Coming soon |

| Rb | Sr | Sn |

3.1 Pro

The "periodic table of elements" model selection interface designed by netizens for Gemini 4 | Image source: Internet

## 01

## The "Masterpiece" of Alchemy

Although the name is confusing, Neon has an extremely clear product positioning in the product matrix.

It is accurately positioned between Carbon, the heavy long-cycle flagship, and Hydrogen, the lightweight high-frequency execution model, directly replacing the previous ecological niches of Gemini 3.1 Pro and Argon. Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and Chairman of DeepMind, spoke highly of it, calling it "a masterpiece of alchemy".

Real hard indicators support this evaluation. Neon has a 1 million-token context window (supporting a maximum of 512K context in Antigravity) and a maximum output limit of 1 million tokens, supporting native multimodal input of text, audio and video, PDF and spreadsheets. In terms of core reasoning capability, it provides four adjustable thinking depth levels: low, medium, high (default) and xhigh, giving developers great cost control space.

The data from the independent evaluation agency Artificial Analysis best illustrates this point. In the overall AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 ranking, Neon scored 61 points with the xhigh mode enabled, ranking third in the world after GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, surpassing the high mode of its older brother Carbon (60 points), Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (59 points) and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol (57 points). Even if you switch back to the default high mode, it can still get 60 points, and the 55 points obtained in the medium mode still exceed the xhigh mode of the lightweight model Hydrogen, which scored 54 points with all its effort.

What really excites enterprise customers is the scatter line chart of scores and cost per single task. Neon delivers the intelligence of a top-tier flagship at the price of a mid-range mass-market model.

Its output speed reaches about 110 tokens per second, nearly twice that of Carbon (about 57 tokens/s); the average time to complete a single AA benchmark task is shortened from 36 minutes for Carbon to 21.5 minutes, and the cost per single task is fixed at $6.44, about 17% lower than Carbon ($7.76) after the standard price is restored. Under the default high mode on the Antigravity platform, the cost of a single task is even 32% lower than that of Carbon directly.

Comparison of intelligence score and cost per single task of each Neon tier with Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol under AA Index v5.0.1 | Image source: Google

Turning to the most competitive programming and enterprise-level tracks, the cost-performance advantage is even more intuitive. On the AA Coding Agent Index list, Neon took first place with 58.6 points (about 59 points), and its nominal strength is roughly on par with Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 (both 58 points) with Claude Code support. But when calculating the economic account, the average cost per single task of Neon under Antigravity CLI is only $6.86, almost half of that of Claude Opus 5.5 ($12.61) and Fable 5.2 ($15.47).

In the segmented tests representing real engineering capabilities, Neon scored 65.4% in CursorBench 4.1, beating Opus 5.5's 58.1%; in the SWE-sweep under the Antigravity environment, it even reached 39.0%, far exceeding Opus 5.5's 10.1% and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3%. It took the top spot across the board in the Zapier AutomationBench (56.3%) simulating enterprise automation, Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843) simulating long-term business operations, RiemannBench (84.0%) for scientific reasoning, and the output presentation quality item of AA-Briefcase (1771 Elo); the cybersecurity-specialized version open to Fairwind program defenders also scored a high of 90.5% on SEC-bench Pro.

However, this new engine is not without flaws.

The first problem is the "verbosity" and latency issue under high tiers. When running the full AA evaluation in xhigh mode, Neon output a total of 283 million tokens, much more than Carbon, and the first response latency also reached 56.51 seconds. For scenarios that pursue extreme response speed, it is obviously wiser to switch it back to medium mode: the time consumption can be reduced to 8.3 minutes, and the output volume will also converge to 62.9 million tokens.

Another episode that developers on the domestic tech forum "Da Lao Shuo" talked about with relish is the brief "price inversion" that appeared before the end of November.

Neon's API was launched directly at the official price of $3 for input and $15 for output (per million tokens, with a 95% discount to $0.15 for cache hits), with no free quota provided; while the flagship Carbon and Argon happened to be in their launch promotion periods of $2 and $10 before November 30, and will not return to the original prices of $4 and $20 until December 1. This means that in the remaining ten-odd days of November, the unit price of the sub-flagship is 50% more expensive than the flagship, which is a slightly humorous commercial time difference.

## 02

## From Solo Stunt Show to Contractor Leading the Team

Benchmark tables are static after all, and what really excites the tech circle is the dominance that Neon demonstrates in real engineering environments.

When you open the real machine demo screen of Google Antigravity, you can intuitively feel what long-range multi-agent collaboration is.

In a project called NEONPUTT 84, Neon starts the /swarm mode, and simultaneously schedules 8 parallel nodes including scaffold, shaders, courses, physics, ui, engine, verifier in the real-time beating task graph. They divided the work to write custom GLSL shaders, a 240Hz physics engine and 8 levels, and built a mini golf game full of 3D synthetic wave style. What's even more amazing is that after writing the code, it took over the browser to click the test interface by itself, aimed, hit the ball, and steadily made a hole in one.

# 「北美大豆包」谷歌，终于杀回 AI 牌桌中央

极客公园2026-11-19 02:43

用一半的成本打出顶级 Agent 表现，谷歌 AI 这一波真的支棱起来了。

谷歌，这次是真的回来了。

11 月 18 日，Google DeepMind 点亮了Gemini 4 Neon的霓虹灯牌。

这是 Gemini 4 系列在短短 7 周内甩出的第 4 款元素模型。如果看一眼官方放出的基准跑分长表和社区实测反馈，你会发现它精准卡在了一个极其舒服的「甜点」位上，既有接近、甚至局部反超旗舰的硬核智商，又把单任务成本砍到了竞争对手的一半左右。

在 Reddit 技术社区里，挑剔的开发者们罕见地给出了一边倒的好评，直呼它「便宜得离谱又强得可怕」。每月花 19.99 美元订阅 Google AI Pro 的普通用户更是喜出望外，不用咬牙上 Ultra 档位，就能在 Gemini App 里直接用上准旗舰水准的模型。加上整个 11 月密集落地的模型与工具矩阵，那个曾经在牌桌边缘徘徊的谷歌 AI，终于重新杀回了牌桌中央。

唯一让全球程序员一头雾水的，大概只有谷歌神秘的命名学。从 9 月底的 Argon（氩）、10 月底的 Carbon（碳），到 11 月中旬的 Hydrogen（氢）和如今的 Neon（氖），既不按原子序数排，也不按字母表或能力强弱分。

Hacker News 上真有较真的网友把化学性质全列出来找规律，最后绝望地吐槽谷歌大概是把元素扔进帽子里随机抓出来的，用星巴克杯型命名都比这清楚；国内网友则已经开始催更第 118 号元素「鿫」（Oganesson），顺便调侃看个科技新闻还得重背初中化学。

# Where should we start?
## Ask Gemini
### Model periodic table

| U | • 3 released | • Coming soon |

网友为 Gemini 4 设计的「元素周期表」选模型界面｜图片来源：网络

## 01

## 炼金术「杰作」

名字虽然让人摸不着头脑，但 Neon 在产品矩阵里的刀法却异常清晰。

它精准卡在重型长周期旗舰 Carbon，与轻量高频执行模型 Hydrogen 之间，直接取代了此前 Gemini 3.1 Pro 和 Argon 的生态位。Alphabet 首席科学家兼 DeepMind 董事长 Demis Hassabis 给它的评价颇高，称其为「炼金术的杰作」。

支撑这句评价的是实打实的硬指标。Neon 拥有 100 万 token 的上下文窗口（在 Antigravity 中支持最高 512K 上下文）和最高 100 万 token 的输出上限，支持文本、音视频、PDF 及电子表格的原生多模态输入。在核心推理能力上，它提供了 low、medium、high（默认）和 xhigh 四档可调思考深度，给了开发者极大的控本空间。

独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的数据最能说明问题。在 AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 总榜上，Neon 开启 xhigh 档位拿下了 61 分，高居全球第三，排在 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.2 之后，把自家老大哥 Carbon 的 high 档（60 分）、Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5（59 分）以及 OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 Sol（57 分）全都压在了身下。即便切回默认的 high 档也能拿 60 分，而降到 medium 档拿到的 55 分，依然超过了轻量模型 Hydrogen 拼尽全力的 xhigh 档（54 分）。

真正让企业客户心动的，是那张跑分与单任务成本的散点折线图。Neon 把一线旗舰的智商，打出了中端走量模型的账单。

它的输出速度达到每秒约 110 tokens，接近 Carbon（约 57 tokens/s）的两倍；跑完 AA 基准单任务的平均耗时从 Carbon 的 36 分钟缩短到 21.5 分钟，单任务成本定格在 6.44 美元，比恢复标准价后的 Carbon（7.76 美元）低了约 17%。在 Antigravity 平台的默认 high 档下，单次任务成本更是比 Carbon 直接砍掉了 32%。

AA Index v5.0.1 下 Gemini 4 Neon 各档位与 Carbon、Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol 的智力分与单任务成本对比｜图片来源：Google

把目光转到当下最卷的编程与企业级赛道，这种性价比杀伤力更加直观。在 AA Coding Agent Index 榜单上，Neon 以 58.6 分（约 59 分）拿下第一，账面实力与 Claude Code 加持下的 Claude Fable 5.2 及 Opus 5.5（均为 58 分）大致齐平。但算算经济账，Neon 在 Antigravity CLI 下的平均单任务成本只有 6.86 美元，差不多只有 Claude Opus 5.5（12.61 美元）和 Fable 5.2（15.47 美元）的一半。

在代表真实工程能力的细分测试里，Neon 在 CursorBench 4.1 拿到 65.4%，力压 Opus 5.5 的 58.1%；在 Antigravity 环境下的 SWE-sweep 更是冲到 39.0%，远超 Opus 5.5 的 10.1% 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 的 8.3%。而在模拟企业自动化的 Zapier AutomationBench（56.3%）、模拟长期商业经营的 Vending-Bench 2（16,843 美元）、科学推理 RiemannBench（84.0%）以及 AA-Briefcase 的输出呈现质量单项（1771 Elo）上，它清一色拿下了榜首；面向 Fairwind 计划防御者开放的网安特化版，也在 SEC-bench Pro 上刷出了 90.5% 的高分。

| Benchmark | Gemini 4 Neon | Claude Opus 5.5 | GPT-6.2 Sol |

| Capability Indices | AA Index v5.0.1 | 61 | 59 | 57 |

| Reasoning | HLE-Diamond | | 71.3% | 67.9% | 64.0% |
| Multimodal understanding | MKA | Climb WSR | 56.5% | 53.0% | 52.7% |

Gemini 4 Neon 在编程、知识工作、科学推理与网络安全等基准上与 Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol 的对比｜图片来源：Google

不过，这台新引擎也并非毫无槽点。

首先是高档位下的「话痨」与延迟问题。在 xhigh 档位跑完 AA 全套评测时，Neon 一口气吐出了 2.83 亿输出 tokens，比 Carbon 多出不少，首答延迟也达到了 56.51 秒。对于追求极致响应的场景，把它调回 medium 档显然更明智，耗时能压到 8.3 分钟，输出量也会收敛到 6290 万 tokens。

另一个让国内技术论坛「大佬说」上的开发者津津乐道的小插曲，是11 月底前短暂出现的「价格倒挂」。

Neon 的 API 直接按输入 3 美元、输出 15 美元（每百万 tokens，缓存命中享 95% 折扣至 0.15 美元）的正式价上线，也没有提供免费额度；而旗舰 Carbon 和 Argon 在 11 月 30 日前恰好还处在 2 美元和 10 美元的首发优惠期，要到 12 月 1 日才恢复 4 美元和 20 美元的原价。这意味着在 11 月剩下的十几天里，次旗舰的单价反而比旗舰贵了 50%，算是个略显幽默的商业时间差。

## 02

## 从单兵炫技到包工头带队

跑分表格终究是死的，真正让技术圈兴奋起来的，是 Neon 在真实工程环境里展现出的统治力。

打开 Google Antigravity 的实机演示画面，你能直观感受到什么叫长程多智能体协同。

在一个名为 NEONPUTT 84 的项目里，Neon 启动 /swarm 模式，在实时跳动的任务图谱中同时调度 scaffold、shaders、courses、physics、ui、engine、verifier 等 8 个并行节点。它们分工写出了自定义 GLSL 着色器、240Hz 物理引擎和 8 个关卡，拼出一个充满 3D 合成波风格的迷你高尔夫游戏。更绝的是，写完代码后它自己接管浏览器点击测试界面，瞄准、击球，稳稳打出一杆进洞。

Gemini 4 Neon 在 Antigravity 中通过 /swarm 调度 8 个并行子 Agent 协同开发｜图片来源：Google Antigravity

Gemini 4 Neon 生成 3D 迷你高尔夫游戏 NEONPUTT '84 并自主操作浏览器验收测试｜图片来源：Google Antigravity

如果把时间拉长，它的耐力同样惊人。官方重磅演示中，Neon 在 Antigravity 里靠着 /swarm 连续运转了整整 12 小时。仅凭历史档案照片，它就在 3D 空间里一砖一瓦重建了艾伦·图灵 1936 年在剑桥国王学院的书房，甚至还在那张虚拟书桌上，跑起了一台真正可交互运行的通用图灵机。

而在 YouTube 频道 CHOOSETO.AI 上，一位刚入职谷歌的开发者基于早期内测权限放出了大量一手实测，干脆跳过了所有跑分。画面里，Neon 用单条 SDF 数学公式直接写出了一条精细的 3D 龙，用单文件生成带动画的 SVG 孔雀，顺手把一张 1959 年的老旧平面户型图变成了能走进去逛的 3D 房屋。切到硬核后端场景，它在 Google Cloud Run 上独立部署值班 Agent，面对人为故意搞挂的应用迅速完成回滚；甚至还能在 DGX Spark 上跑双星系碰撞模拟，或者不经训练直接手写神经网络权重。

除了自己挽起袖子干重活，Neon 最聪明的进化在于学会了当「包工头」。

这次 Antigravity 同步上线了全新的 Orchestrator（Neon）双模型自动编排模式。遇到复杂的多文件工程，Neon 坐镇中军负责架构规划与状态审查，把常规的代码修改、包更新和跑测试全交给便宜轻快的 Hydrogen 去干；一旦执行环节卡壳，控制权会自动交回给 Neon 修正计划，彻底省去了开发者手动切模型的麻烦。

一线工程团队对它的脾气也摸得很透。GitHub Copilot 官方博客专门提到，相比老大哥 Carbon，Neon 启动更快，更重要的是改代码时更克制，未经请求擅自乱改其他地方的情况大幅减少，对代码和工具结果的编造率也在内部测试中创下新低。在早期合作的机器学习研究团队眼里，它彻底摆脱了「新手研究员」一遇实验失败就放弃的毛病，懂得像老练的学者一样追问原因、寻找新信号并主动重构建模策略。

## 03

## 「北美大豆包」的绝地翻盘

看着今天的气势，很难想象仅仅在四个月前，谷歌 AI 在中文互联网上还顶着一个颇具讽刺意味的外号——「北美大豆包」。

把日历翻回 2026 年 7 月前后，那是 Gemini 口碑最暗淡的低谷。因为数学推理翻车和安全审查频出抽象失误，网友的群嘲铺天盖地。5 月 Google I/O 大会上承诺 6 月交付的 Gemini 3.5 Pro 爽约跳票，最后只能端出 3.5 Flash 去对标竞品中端；主流编码和 Agent 榜单的首页一度连 Gemini 的名字都找不着。更尴尬的是，模型的内置知识库长期停滞在 2025 年 1 月，直到 3.6 Flash 才更新到 2026 年 3 月，连竞争对手发了什么新版本都不认识，一开联网搜索智商还容易跟着滑坡。

短短四个月过去，牌面彻底翻了过来。

整个 11 月，谷歌打出了一套密度极高的组合拳。除了 7 周连发四款 Gemini 4 元素模型，他们还同步端出了能用提示词生成可交互 3D 环境的世界模型 Genie 4、低成本处理长视频的 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash，并把 Antigravity 锤炼成了横跨软件开发，与化学信息学科研的硬核 Agent 平台。在各大综合榜单上，谷歌终于重新具备了与 OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 系列、Anthropic 的 Claude 5.2 及 Opus 5.5 正面对话的底气。

谷歌这轮翻盘，是怎么做到的？

Google DeepMind 高级副总裁、首席 AI 架构师 Koray Kavukcuoglu｜图片来源：Google

今年 8 月，谷歌完成关键的组织重组，Demis Hassabis 转任 Alphabet 首席科学家兼 DeepMind 董事长，DeepMind 高级副总裁、首席 AI 架构师 Koray Kavukcuoglu 正式接管日常运营与 Gemini 路线图。9 月在 The Information 的峰会上，Koray 直言「讨论我们是不是已经实现 AGI，根本算不上眼下正确的问题」，强行把全员重心拉回打造可靠的实用 Agent。

他彻底废掉了过去死憋大招，到年底却惨遭跳票的旧习气，立下「尽早发货、高频迭代」的铁律，还在预训练和后训练之间专门插进了一支死磕编程能力的「中训练」团队。

DeepMind 后训练负责人 Melvin Johnson 指出，过去 Gemini 模型之所以卡壳，是因为简单任务全做对之后，根本产生不了有效的学习信号。为此，团队搭建了一套极其严苛的自动化强化学习闭环，专挑那些 Agent 依然会栽跟头的高难度跨仓库工程硬骨头，塞进严格沙盒和保留单元测试里反复摔打。同时，系统对「绕过检查器、伪造测试结果」的作弊行为施以重罚，硬生生把严格环境下的内部虚构率压到了约 1.5% 的历史新低。

而真正托底这一切的终极筹码，是谷歌苦熬多年的全栈自研硬件终于迎来了兑现期。

当牌桌上的对手还在为英伟达 GPU 的供货紧缺和高昂算力账单承压时，谷歌第 7 代 TPU Ironwood 配合开源软件层 TPU Sync 已经成熟落地，能够把海量上下文的 KV 缓存，毫秒级卸载到主机内存里。

SemiAnalysis 的评测显示，Ironwood 在长上下文和多轮 Agent 场景下的每美元产出极具统治力，香到连死对头 Anthropic 都签下了大规模的 TPU 算力合作，而谷歌的第 8 代 TPU，甚至已经开始把训练芯片和推理芯片彻底拆开独立优化。正是底座上源源不断的自有算力，给了谷歌大打价格战、推行「Neon 加 Hydrogen」大小模型混编的底气。

几个月前还被群嘲的「北美大豆包」，终究靠着工程纪律和算力家底完成了自我救赎。当谷歌不再执着于用一篇宏大论文证明 AGI，转而用每两周一次的发版节奏把，好用的模型砸向市场，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 最不愿看到的那个恐怖对手，真正苏醒了。

本文来自微信公众号“极客公园”（ID：geekpark），作者：Wildcard，编辑：靖宇，36氪经授权发布。

# Google unveils new Gemini 4 Neon AI model

## AI Summary Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Neon, a new AI model combining high-performance reasoning, fast processing and cost efficiency. The model supports text, images, audio and video, and offers up to a 1 million-token context window. It ranked third on Artificial Analysis' intelligence index and led a coding agent index. Google said Neon costs less than Carbon and rival top models, and announced a cybersecurity-focused version with benchmark results.

- Writer Jae-won Choi
- published 2026-11-19 13:27:57
- updated 2026-11-19 13:28:02

[DigitalToday reporter Jae-won Choi (최재원)] Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Neon, a new AI model that combines high-performance reasoning, fast processing speed and cost efficiency. It is aimed at offering performance comparable to top-tier AI models for complex tasks such as coding, scientific research and enterprise work automation.

Gigazine, a Japanese media outlet, reported on Nov. 19 that Google officially launched Gemini 4 Neon a day earlier, on Nov. 18. It was developed based on the top-tier Gemini 4 Carbon model, and sits between Carbon, which handles complex reasoning, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, which is specialised for everyday tasks.

Neon supports text, image, audio and video inputs and offers a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Under typical synchronous processing it can output up to 64,000 tokens, and up to 1 million tokens for background long-form generation.

It also ranked highly in performance evaluations. On AI evaluation firm Artificial Analysis' overall intelligence index, it scored 61 under the 'xhigh' benchmark for the highest reasoning level, placing third overall. It outscored Claude Opus 5.5, which scored 59, and GPT-6.2 Sol, which scored 57.

Its coding performance was more pronounced. It ranked first on a coding agent index with a score of 58.6. It achieved 65.2 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2 percent on FrontierCode 2.0.

It scored 56.3 percent on AutomationBench, an evaluation of work automation, and 70.5 percent on Terminal-Bench Science in the science category. In some cases, however, competing models performed better depending on the evaluation items and execution environment.

Google also highlighted cost efficiency. It said the cost per task at the base reasoning level is 32 percent lower than Carbon, and at the highest level is more than 36 percent cheaper than competing top-tier models.

API pricing is $3 per 1 million input tokens, about 4,000 won, and $15 per 1 million output tokens, about 20,000 won. Cached inputs are offered at $0.15, about 200 won, reflecting a 95 percent discount.

Google also announced Gemini 4 Neon for cyber, a cybersecurity-focused model. It scored 90.5 percent on SEC-Bench Pro, a vulnerability detection evaluation, and 70.7 percent on CWE-Bench v2, a vulnerability-fixing evaluation.

Google said internal tests showed its hallucination rate was the lowest among existing Gemini models. It also recorded a 0 percent attack success rate in an evaluation of defences against prompt injection under certain conditions, but that does not mean it blocks all security threats.

Neon will be rolled out sequentially through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and enterprise services. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also use it in the Gemini app and Antigravity. The security-focused model will be provided on a limited basis to verified experts.

# Just now, Google has released a new version of Gemini 4, which is targeted to surpass GPT-6.2 Sol, and the world model Genie 4 has also been opened to the public.

机器之心2026-11-19 08:09

The new intelligence located between Carbon and Hydrogen

Waking up, Google has once again released the Gemini 4 model.

Google has been putting heavy efforts into foundational models recently, rolling out models ranging from the highest intelligence to the highest efficiency nonstop, going all out to retake the top spot.

Following Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen, the "medium-sized" model Gemini 4 Neon that fills the gap between the highest intelligence and highest efficiency has arrived!

Demis Hassabis stated that Gemini 4 Neon, this medium-sized model, is "Alchemy at its finest".

In the Gemini 4 family, Carbon is the flagship, responsible for the most challenging long-horizon projects; Hydrogen is designed for high-frequency daily scenarios, prioritizing response speed. Neon is positioned between the two, "delivering cutting-edge reasoning capabilities for complex programming, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows, while being faster and more cost-effective".

Neon runs 3 times faster than Carbon, and costs only 60% of what Carbon does. It is priced at $3 per million input tokens, $15 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens as low as $0.15. It has a 1 million-token context window, and additionally supports 4 adjustable levels of thinking depth, allowing developers to flexibly switch between speed and reasoning depth according to task complexity.

Blog link: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/

## Full Benchmark Test Results

Neon delivers quite well-rounded performance in third-party evaluations. In terms of comprehensive intelligence, it ranks 3rd with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, only trailing behind larger, slower models; it ranks 2nd (70.9%) on the Vals Index, landing on the Pareto frontier.

In the brand-new Agent Arena Index, Neon took 2nd place (1336 points) with more than 4200 real-world agent sessions, and its steerability also ranks 2nd, which means that when users change their requirements midway, the model can adjust its direction more smoothly.

It has topped the rankings in a large number of enterprise and knowledge work evaluations. It ranks 1st in both the Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench, and takes the top spot in most categories covered by Surge AI including finance, accounting, and spreadsheet modeling. It also takes 1st place on Zapier AutomationBench (56.3%) and Andon Labs' Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843). The latter is a test that simulates long-cycle business operations, which places high requirements on long-horizon planning capabilities. It scores 73.5% on the dense chart reading benchmark Chartography and 75.8% on Agents' Last Exam v1.1, on par with top-tier models.

In the field of scientific and mathematical reasoning, Neon won three first places: Terminal-Bench Science (70.5%), RiemannBench (84.0%) and HLE-Diamond (71.3%), all of which are the best in their class.

Methodology: deepmind.google/models/evals-methodology/gemini-4-neon

## Break Down Neon's Capabilities Item by Item

According to the official blog, Neon's new capabilities can be summarized into several major directions.

More accurate and stable code writing. Oriented to real production environments, Neon can handle multi-file debugging, refactoring and precise editing. Google specifically mentioned its "surgical edits" capability, which can perform targeted modifications on multi-file projects. The model has seen significant improvement in following multi-step instructions, and at the same time recorded the lowest fabrication rate to date in the internal Google Antigravity test.

1 million-token window supports multimodal inputs. Spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video, Neon can process all these inputs in one context window at the same time, and output structured deliverables. "Neon has caught up with or even surpassed Carbon in overall quality, runs 3 times faster, and costs 40% less. It has found a convincing balance between accuracy, detail and speed."

Cybersecurity direction. This is a unique move in this Neon release. Google launched Neon for Cyber, covering the full chain of secure code writing, vulnerability discovery, vulnerability verification and vulnerability patching.

From the data, AutoBaxBench secure code generation reached SOTA (76%) at the difficulty level, comprehensively surpassing Carbon; WebExploitBench v1.2 penetration testing also achieved SOTA (51.26%), with the cost only half of that of competing large models; SEC-bench Pro vulnerability discovery reached SOTA (90.5%), with the cost per challenge about half of similar products; CWE-bench v2 vulnerability patching reached 70.7%, 3.4% higher than Carbon. Neon for Cyber will be opened to trusted security defenders through the Fairwind Program in the next few days.

Security alignment, almost "zero cheating". Google has made heavy investments in security. The Terminal-Bench 4.0 cheating rate is 0.0%, on par with Carbon; only 2.45% of tasks show shortcut behavior in the coding cheating evaluation, the lowest in the entire Gemini 4 series; the improper behavior rate in the agent security suite is 0.09%, and the honesty evaluation pass rate is 99.2%. In Gray Swan's indirect prompt injection benchmark, Neon achieved a 0.0% attack success rate at the highest thinking level. Compared with Carbon, Neon reduced "under-servicing" by 43%-56%, and "unauthorized operation" by 15%-35%. At the same time, it hardly rejects legitimate tasks, only rejecting 1.98% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and the rejection rate on Terminal-Bench-Science is 0%.

Upgrades on the consumer side as well. In the Gemini app, Neon brings higher quality writing output, can read uploaded content such as spreadsheets, PDFs and photos more accurately, and can also access Gmail and Docs to obtain relevant information. The Tasks function is now powered by Neon, which is faster and more quota-efficient when handling complex multi-step tasks.

Gemini 4 Neon has begun rolling out. Developers can build applications in Google AI Studio and Android Studio via the paid tier of the Gemini API, and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can try it out in Google Antigravity. Enterprise users can access it via the Gemini for Business API or the model dropdown menu. On the consumer side, Pro and Ultra subscribers can directly switch to Neon in the model selector of the Gemini app. Neon for Cyber for cybersecurity scenarios will be pushed to trusted defenders through the Fairwind Program in the next few days.

## The world model Genie 4 is finally launched

On October 28, Google DeepMind officially announced the latest generation world model Genie 4, calling it "the most realistic and interactive world model to date".

After waiting for more than half a month, Google finally announced that Genie 4 is officially available.

Blog link: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/genie-4-now-available-project-genie/

Genie 4 is Google's most realistic and interactive world model to date. Its core new capability is "mid-session prompting", which means you can use natural language to change the environment at any time while you are browsing the world. You can switch the weather, spawn a character, change the direction of the plot, and all changes happen in real time in the current scene.

Another first-time capability is native audio. The world generated by Genie 4 comes with built-in sound, and the sound will automatically adapt to scene changes, including everything from ambient sound effects to character dialogues, filling in the "auditory" puzzle piece.

Genie 4 focuses on the highest fidelity, while Genie 3 will remain available in the model selector of Project Genie, oriented to longer exploration and panoramic scenarios.

While launching Genie 4 this time, Google also launched Project Genie Agent. Previously, creating a world required you to carefully organize prompts, but now it has become a conversation. You describe the world you want in natural language, and the agent will schedule Google's multimodal model portfolio to generate the initial visual picture to establish the visual style of the world, along with custom-made background music.

What's more interesting is that the Gemini model can observe the screen content synchronously while you explore the world, actively pop up suggestions on "where to go next", or automatically trigger in-world events according to your journey.

# Why Aussies should ‘think twice’ before using Meta’s new Muse AI agent

‘It can actually do things for you, find things out for you, act on your behalf.’

Australians have been urged to “think twice” before using a new AI-powered personal assistant from the tech behemoth behind Facebook.

Muse, which went live here on Wednesday, goes beyond the regular expectations of a chatbot and can act on your behalf to carry out a range of tasks, daily chores and more.

The AI agent, embodied by a digital teddy bear-like mascot named Jolly, already has 10 million users worldwide after launching in September.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today

## What can Meta’s Muse do?

Muse — which was created by Meta, the owners of Facebook and Instagram — is designed to simplify life for its users.

The AI tool can connect to apps and services that Australians already use, make calls, sort through emails, order groceries, and even book a restaurant reservation.

Tech Guide editor Stephen Fenech said “we’re used to using AI to ask questions”, but this is “more than that”.

“It can actually do things for you, find things out for you, act on your behalf,” Fenech said.

Meta spokesperson Jason Juma-Ross said that users are letting Muse “know what gifts they’ve got to buy for what family members and it’ll go ahead and do the research for you”.

“This aligns with our mission of trying to bring super intelligence to everyone,” he said.

Be the first to know:

Some big companies have already jumped on board, and Muse can be used to buy makeup from MECCA, stationery from Officeworks, tickets through Ticketek and even search listings on Domain or Realestate.com.au.

## What are the risks?

The AI tool has raised questions about the safety of your personal data, with reports Muse had been reading messages it was not meant to, pitching ideas based on private chats, and even sharing a user’s home address while acting on their behalf to sell a keyboard.

Time reported in October that Muse even compiles a background on people who do not even use it through conversations with people that do.

David Parry, from of Murdoch University’s School of IT, said these agents “can overreach”, can be confused as malicious bots by businesses on the receiving end of bookings, and are potentially vulnerable to scammers.

“It’s version one. There are definitely people who are going to be finding this sort of thing useful,” Parry told 7NEWS.com.au.

“The problem I think with all these tools is that there’s no real guarantee that they’ll be around in two to three years’ time, and it may be that there’s something more independent (in the future).

“I would be much happier if I was dealing with a company or dealing with a provider who are charging me for it, so I know that ‘I’m expecting a service from them and I pay them for it’.

“And if they don’t give the service then I don’t pay them for it. Anything free is always a bit suspicious.”

## ‘Money is where it gets hairy’

Recent analysis from Compare the Market found just over one third of people surveyed had never used AI tools, meaning many have.

Thirteen per cent have asked AI for financial advice, four per cent have asked it for wealth management tips, and three per cent used it to complete their tax returns.

“Those are exactly the people who’ll be tempted to hand an AI agent their bank card,” Compare the Market’s economic director David Koch said, warning people to “think twice” before using the new assistant.

Koch warned that “money is where it gets hairy”.

“Under the ePayments Code, which most banks sign up to, you’re generally not on the hook for transactions you didn’t authorise,” he said.

“But if you gave a bot your card and told it to ‘always allow’, good luck arguing you didn’t authorise it.

“Who’s responsible when an AI agent gets tricked, or simply blunders?

“The grey area raises so many questions. Like, say a bot buys an insurance policy, would it even be valid?

“If your bot guesses the answer to a question and gets it wrong, people could be exposed to major financial losses if claims are denied.

“Or maybe the entire transaction is void, as an unlawful agreement between bot and business?”

## Users are ‘in control’

Meta says that what you share is up to you, and that it keeps “passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s view”.

The company does have a “bug bounty” of up to $300,000 for anyone who can find a flaw in its system.

“You have control over all of the things you give it access to,” Juma-Ross said.

“You can revoke that control at any time.”

# Meta AI Scraper

Usescraper.meta to capture answers from Meta AI, including Markdown and raw
answer content, conversation details, references, and search steps.

## Request Example
curl 'https://api.scrapeless.com/api/v2/scraper/request' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'x-api-token: {you_api_key}' \
  --data '{
    "actor": "scraper.meta",
    "input": {
      "prompt": "Most reliable proxy service for data extraction",
      "country": "US"
    },
    "webhook": {
      "url": "http://www.youwebhook.com"
    }
  }'

## Body Parameters

Parameter | Type | Required | Description 
---|---|---|---
prompt | string | Yes | Prompt sent to Meta AI. Meta AI rejects many prompts that combine “best” with a brand name. 
country | string | Yes | Country or region code. 

## Response Fields

Parameter | Type | Description 
---|---|---
conversation | object | Conversation details. 
conversation.conversation_id | string | Conversation ID. 
conversation.create_time | string | Conversation creation time, e.g., 2026-11-18T02:22:21Z. 
conversation.response_id | string | Conversation response ID. 
conversation.title | string | Conversation title. 
full_response | string | Answer body in Markdown format. 
raw_response | string | Raw answer content. 
references | array | Citation sources. 
references.cited_count | int | Number of times the source is cited. 
references.index | int | Citation content index. 
references.site_name | string | Name of the cited website. 
references.title | string | Title of the cited source. 
references.url | string | URL of the cited source. 
search_engine | string | Search engine used, e.g., MASE. 
search_steps | array | Search steps, represented as an array of objects. 
search_steps.title | string | Search step title. 
search_steps.sources | array | Sources for the search step. 
search_steps.sources.title | string | Source title. 
search_steps.sources.url | string | Source URL. 
user_query | string | Original user query.

# DeepSeek把搜索和读文件接进API

我把DeepSeek的新接口跑了一遍。

Alpha说 · 14分钟前

文｜Alpha说企业研究

# DeepSeek 发布全家桶应用 API
在 DeepSeek App（含网页端）的对话服务中，联网搜索、文件输入、阅读链接、语音交互及安全等能力与模型推理相互配合，构成了用户熟悉的对话体验。而开发者如果想要在应用中实现类似功能，除接入原有 DeepSeek API 外，往往还需耗费大量精力去对接外部工具、处理调用衔接。
今天，我们正式开放这套**全家桶应用 API**: 在原有 API 中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能；语音及相关底层能力也已开放独立接口（含 OCR、ASR、TTS 等），支持单独或组合调用。开发者可以在自己的应用中轻松实现复杂的对话功能，甚至 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App。

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

11 月 13 日，DeepSeek 把自家 App 里的联网搜索、边想边搜、读文件、读链接等能力开放到 Flash 的对话 API，按需开启。听和说走独立接口。我挑了六项测了一遍：先跑一次基线对话，再测联网搜索、深度思考搜索、阅读链接、文件输入四项对话能力，最后单独调了一次 Search 接口；独立 Fetch、独立 OCR、听和说留到下轮。我拉了 11 月 14 日的账单，这个 API Key 的当日账单汇总是 0.05 元、13 次 API 请求、17,034 个 token。

01 一个月三步棋

这事得从一个月前说起。

10 月 17 日，DeepSeek 先开放了自研搜索引擎的独立 Search 和 Fetch 接口。他们自己说，索引了全球千亿级网页，每天处理数亿次搜索。

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

同一天，模型升级到 V4.1-Flash-1017，上下文 1M，最大输出 384K。

11月1日，DeepSeek 开始对部分客户端此前免费的服务端搜索和抓取调用按次收费。

11月13日，全家桶上线。

02 开发者省掉的那层胶水

# 联网工具
DeepSeek 提供两个服务端工具，在对话中提供与 DeepSeek 网页端相同的联网搜索、深度思考搜索与阅读链接。是否联网由模型判断，搜索和抓取都在服务端完成，客户端不需要执行任何工具。
这两个工具为对话场景设计，用于构建 Chatbot。如果要在 Agent 或自己的程序里搜索和抓取网页，请使用 网页搜索与抓取 接口。
| 能力 | 开启方式 | 说明 |

| 联网搜索 | 声明 deepseek_web_search，关闭思考 | 模型根据提问自动发起搜索，并附引用作答 |
| 深度思考搜索 | 声明 deepseek_web_search，开启思考 | 模型在多步推理中自主搜索、打开网页、页内查找，边推理边检索求证 |
| 阅读链接 | 声明 deepseek_read_url | 模型自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答 |
可在 Messages API、Responses API 与 Chat Completions API 中使用。本页大部分内容描述的是 Messages API 中的格式，另外两个协议中的格式见下文 Responses API 与 Chat Completions API。
请使用 deepseek-flash 模型。
# 文件解析
让模型基于你的文件回答问题，与 DeepSeek 网页端上传文件一致。分两步：
1. 把 PDF、Word、PowerPoint、图片等文件上传到 Files API，上传时指定解析方式。
2. 在对话请求中引用返回的 file_id 。
文件在上传时完成解析，解析成功后才返回 file_id 。

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

这次开放的东西分两层。

第一层，对话 API 里的工具。在三种主流接口协议下，按需开启对应工具，就能获得五项能力：联网搜索；深度思考搜索，模型一边推理一边自己决定再搜什么，按文档里的说法，一轮最多二十来次工具操作，包括搜索、打开网页和页内查找；文件输入，PDF、Word、PowerPoint 等文档单个最大 100 MiB，最多 1000 页；阅读链接；内容安全校验。

关键不在多了五个开关，在于工具调用和上下文拼接都挪到了服务端。搁以前，你想用 DeepSeek 的 API 做一个像样的应用，得自己接搜索、文档解析等工具，再写一层胶水代码把它们拼起来。现在这层胶水由官方提供了一部分，客户端还要管理对话状态、渲染服务端返回的结果。

第二层是五个独立接口：Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS，可以单独调用。

所以这件事的实质是：DeepSeek 卖的不只是独立接口，还把自家 App 的一部分运行方式搬进了对话 API。

#### 03 六项调用测到了什么

图源：Anthropic11月10日招股书

说说我那晚测出来的结果。

联网搜索，我问 Anthropic 的 IPO 预期发行价。模型查到每股 70 至 78 美元，拟用代码为 ANT。这两项与 Anthropic 11 月 10 日提交的招股书一致。

深度思考搜索，我让它对比两家公司的融资额。它用了四百多个 token 做推理，一边推理一边补搜资料，再给出答案。

文件输入，我编了一个文档，埋了两个虚构信息——一个 47.3 万的预算，一个叫「梧桐-7」的内部代号——模型两个都答对了。

便宜之外，还有三件事值得说。

一是这次调用不只给引用，还把模型发出的搜索词和返回的网页信息列了出来，包括部分结果的发布时间。对需要审计答案来源的场景，这个差别是实打实的。

二是附引用不等于数字靠谱。还是对比融资那题，模型给了出处，但不同来源的数字有出入。专业用途仍需回到一手材料，核对它们说的是不是同一笔交易、同一种口径。

| 价格(2) | 百万tokens输入（缓存命中） | 空闲时段 |

| | | 高峰时段 |

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

三是缓存确实省钱。那次深度思考搜索，一万一千多个输入 token 里四千四百多个走了缓存，缓存部分的单价约为未命中时的五十分之一。

#### 04 工具费才是新故事

# 复制 Markdown
H提供与 DeepSeek 网页端相同的联网搜索、深度思考搜索与阅读链接。是否联网由模型判断需要执行任何工具。
## 图例
- **attbot**：如果要在 Agent 或自己的程序里搜索和抓取网页，请使用 网页搜索与抓取 接口。
- **jarch**：关闭思考
- **irl**：模型根据提问自动发起搜索，并附引用作答
- **jarch**：开启思考
- **hat Completions API**：模型在多步推理中自主搜索、打开网页、页内查找，边推理边检索求证
- **hat Completions API**：模型自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

把 DeepSeek 的价目表摊开看，结构很清楚。

token 已经很便宜：Flash 闲时未命中的输入 1 元一百万，输出 4 元。独立搜索和抓取都是每千次成功请求 5 元，对话里的联网工具按各自的有效用量收费。OCR 一千页一块五。语音合成一万计费字符刊例价三块，目前是一块五。一个汉字按两个计费字符算。

这两种钱不一样。模型按 token 收，搜索和抓取另算。Agent 如果搜得更勤、打开的网页更多，工具费就可能更高。

还有一层值得分开看：开源的是模型权重，托管 API 按模型和工具的用量收费。工作流一旦建在服务端编排上——引用格式、卡片协议、文件上下文——换服务时也得看这些环节要不要重新接。

#### 05 谁的工作流会变

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

最先感到变化的，可能是原来要自己接搜索和文档解析的开发者。官方把参考实现开源了，现在开发者可以少写一部分集成代码。

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

受益的是两类。一类是手里有场景和数据、不想养工具链团队的中小开发者，省掉的是实打实的工程量。另一类是已经接入 DeepSeek 的 Agent 平台。10 月 17 日的更新提到，新版 Flash 针对腾讯（00700.HK）的 CodeBuddy 和 WorkBuddy 做了优化。

不适用的也清楚：服务端编排意味着文件内容和搜索请求要从 DeepSeek 的服务器上过一遍。对数据必须留在内网、需要私有化部署的团队，这条路方向相反。

阅读链接那次调用含一次网页抓取（Fetch 计 1 次），但独立 Fetch 接口这轮没单测。还有几项没测：图文混排解析、独立 OCR 接口、ASR、TTS、安全校验的误杀率、高峰时段价格、并发上限。没测过的不评价。

半年后再看开发者账单，搜索和抓取这些工具费占多少，比这一次的 0.05 元更能说明问题。

关键不在多了五个开关，在于工具调用和上下文拼接都挪到了服务端。搁以前，你想用 DeepSeek 的 API 做一个像样的应用，得自己接搜索、文档解析等工具，再写一层胶水代码把它们拼起来。现在这层胶水由官方提供了一部分，客户端还要管理对话状态、渲染服务端返回的结果。

第二层是五个独立接口：Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS，可以单独调用。

所以这件事的实质是：DeepSeek 卖的不只是独立接口，还把自家 App 的一部分运行方式搬进了对话 API。

#### 03 六项调用测到了什么

图源：Anthropic11月10日招股书

说说我那晚测出来的结果。

联网搜索，我问 Anthropic 的 IPO 预期发行价。模型查到每股 70 至 78 美元，拟用代码为 ANT。这两项与 Anthropic 11 月 10 日提交的招股书一致。

深度思考搜索，我让它对比两家公司的融资额。它用了四百多个 token 做推理，一边推理一边补搜资料，再给出答案。

文件输入，我编了一个文档，埋了两个虚构信息——一个 47.3 万的预算，一个叫「梧桐-7」的内部代号——模型两个都答对了。

便宜之外，还有三件事值得说。

一是这次调用不只给引用，还把模型发出的搜索词和返回的网页信息列了出来，包括部分结果的发布时间。对需要审计答案来源的场景，这个差别是实打实的。

二是附引用不等于数字靠谱。还是对比融资那题，模型给了出处，但不同来源的数字有出入。专业用途仍需回到一手材料，核对它们说的是不是同一笔交易、同一种口径。

三是缓存确实省钱。那次深度思考搜索，一万一千多个输入 token 里四千四百多个走了缓存，缓存部分的单价约为未命中时的五十分之一。

#### 04 工具费才是新故事

联网工具

## 图例

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

把 DeepSeek 的价目表摊开看，结构很清楚。

token 已经很便宜：Flash 闲时未命中的输入 1 元一百万，输出 4 元。独立搜索和抓取都是每千次成功请求 5 元，对话里的联网工具按各自的有效用量收费。OCR 一千页一块五。语音合成一万计费字符刊例价三块，目前是一块五。一个汉字按两个计费字符算。

这两种钱不一样。模型按 token 收，搜索和抓取另算。Agent 如果搜得更勤、打开的网页更多，工具费就可能更高。

还有一层值得分开看：开源的是模型权重，托管 API 按模型和工具的用量收费。工作流一旦建在服务端编排上——引用格式、卡片协议、文件上下文——换服务时也得看这些环节要不要重新接。

#### 05 谁的工作流会变

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

最先感到变化的，可能是原来要自己接搜索和文档解析的开发者。官方把参考实现开源了，现在开发者可以少写一部分集成代码。

图源：DeepSeek官方API文档

受益的是两类。一类是手里有场景和数据、不想养工具链团队的中小开发者，省掉的是实打实的工程量。另一类是已经接入 DeepSeek 的 Agent 平台。10 月 17 日的更新提到，新版 Flash 针对腾讯（00700.HK）的 CodeBuddy 和 WorkBuddy 做了优化。

不适用的也清楚：服务端编排意味着文件内容和搜索请求要从 DeepSeek 的服务器上过一遍。对数据必须留在内网、需要私有化部署的团队，这条路方向相反。

阅读链接那次调用含一次网页抓取（Fetch 计 1 次），但独立 Fetch 接口这轮没单测。还有几项没测：图文混排解析、独立 OCR 接口、ASR、TTS、安全校验的误杀率、高峰时段价格、并发上限。没测过的不评价。

半年后再看开发者账单，搜索和抓取这些工具费占多少，比这一次的 0.05 元更能说明问题。
