# Grok 4.8 有好幾個型號？內測裏多條變體，廣發還沒定哪條

作者注：馬斯克在 2026-11-19 說“Grok 4.8”現在是好幾條內測變體，廣發用哪條還沒定。本文梳理他的原話、官方型號列表與價格，說明今天調 Grok 應該用 grok-4.7。

如果你已經在接口裏用 Grok 寫代碼、做問答，這兩天大概率刷到了馬斯克關於 Grok 4.8 的帖子，並且想知道能不能把請求裏的model 改成 4.8。2026-11-19 北京時間 09:28，馬斯克本人回覆了一條剪輯視頻，原話是 “Grok 4.8” is currently several different model variants in beta。也就是說，這個名字底下目前是好幾條內測變體，最後廣發哪一條還沒有定。

這不是坊間傳言，下文引用的都是馬斯克本人賬號的原文，以及 xAI 官方模型列表在 2026-11-19 的頁面內容。剪輯號的口播會單獨標爲轉寫，不作爲公告。

核心價值：讀完本文你會知道：今天先別在代碼裏寫死一個叫 Grok 4.8 的模型 ID。現在要調 Grok，請用型號列表裏的grok-4.7。

Table of Contents

## Grok 4.8 有好幾個型號：核心信息速覽

先給結論：截至 2026-11-19，Grok 4.8 還不是一個可以在接口裏調用的模型 ID。馬斯克說它目前是幾條處於 beta 階段的變體，廣發哪一條尚未確定。xAI 官方模型列表裏也沒有grok-4.8。

信息項 | 截至 2026-11-19 的情況 | 對調用方意味着什麼 
---|---|---
Grok 4.8 是什麼 | 馬斯克原話：好幾條不同的內測變體，還沒確定哪條廣發 | 名字背後沒有一個固定的模型 
誰能用到 | 一部分 Grok Bot 用戶被小範圍放量試用 | Bot 裏抽到試用，不代表接口裏有這個型號 
何時廣發 | 馬斯克估計廣發前還要打磨“一兩週” | 這是口頭估計，不是發佈日 
官方模型列表 | 沒有 grok-4.8，最新旗艦是 grok-4.7 | 今天寫進請求的應該是 grok-4.7 
官方價格 | 沒有 4.8 的模型卡、價格和發佈日 | 無法爲 4.8 做成本預算 

### Grok 4.8 原話梳理：最近三條帖說了什麼

最近兩天的信息大多來自馬斯克本人在 X 上的回覆。按時間排列看，幾條帖子之間並不矛盾，而是一步步把情況說得更具體。下表的時間都換算成了北京時間。

時間（北京時間） | 來源 | 內容 | 性質 
---|---|---|---
11-18 01:56 | 馬斯克本人 | “Grok 4.8 has not rolled out for general use yet， just some trials behind the scenes.” | 原話：沒對一般用戶放開，只有幕後試用 
11-18 02:29 | 馬斯克本人 | “We did do a soft rollout to some Bot users， but still have another week or two of polish before general release.” | 原話：已對部分 Bot 用戶小範圍放量，廣發前再打磨一兩週 
11-19 07:55 | 剪輯號 @firesidealpha | 視頻配文：在做 Grok 4.8，處於 RL 階段，會在 Grok Bot 裏週期性小範圍放量，用戶有時用到的是底下不同版本 | 剪輯號轉寫的口播，不是 xAI 公告 
11-19 09:28 | 馬斯克本人 | “”Grok 4.8″ is currently several different model variants in beta. We’re not yet sure which of the variants will go to wide release.” | 原話：好幾條內測變體，廣發哪條未定 

前兩條只相隔 33 分鐘。第一條說“一般用戶還沒有”，第二條補充“部分 Bot 用戶有試用”，兩句話說的是不同人羣。第四條是本週的新信息：馬斯克直接說“Grok 4.8”這個名字當前對應好幾條變體。

### Grok 4.8 爲什麼還不是一個模型 ID

剪輯號轉寫的口播提到，Bot 用戶有時用到的是底下不同的版本，團隊會看這些版本能不能解決用戶的問題，再用結果繼續改。這段只能當作轉寫來理解，但它和馬斯克 11-19 的原話方向一致。“Grok 4.8”現在更像一個研發代號，而不是一個已經凍結的模型。

接口裏的模型 ID 需要對應一個確定的模型，同時要有確定的價格、上下文長度和端點。幾條變體還在內測篩選，任何一條都可能不是最終廣發的版本。所以現在爲“Grok 4.8”找一個可調用的 ID 沒有意義，也找不到。在官方列表上線之前，自己拼一個grok-4.8 寫進請求，結果大概率是報錯。

還有一點值得注意：馬斯克說的“再一兩週”是在北京時間 11-18 凌晨（UTC 11 月 17 日）給出的估計。他在 11-19 又說廣發哪條變體還沒定。把這兩句話放在一起看，“一兩週”只能當作參考，不能當作排期依據。

## 今天調 Grok 用 grok-4.7：查型號、對價格、對調用地址

既然 4.8 還沒有落成型號，今天要做的就是三件事：確認型號列表，覈對價格，配好調用地址。下面按順序說明。

### 第一步：在型號列表裏查 Grok 4.8 和 grok-4.7

2026-11-19 打開 xAI 官方模型頁，頁面上沒有grok-4.8，最新旗艦是 grok-4.7。代碼和對話兩類場景的推薦型號也都指向 Grok 4.7。

聚合平臺這一側同樣可以覈對。API易 的實時定價接口api.apiyi.com/api/pricing 在 2026-11-19 拉取時共有 285 個型號，裏面沒有 grok-4.8，也沒有任何帶 4.8 字樣的變體名。同名的 grok-4.7 只有一條，沒有官轉、官逆或 all 後綴的相鄰通道。它的可用分組是 CodexResponses、Default 和 SVIP。

還要提醒一點：grok-4.7 目前沒有單獨的說明頁，查它的信息要看型號總表。上一代 grok-4.6 有自己的說明頁，但它的階梯分界和 4.7 不一樣，不要混用。

### 第二步：覈對 grok-4.7 的價格（官方與 API易 分開看）

官方價格和平臺價格來自兩個不同的頁面，數據日期也不同，所以分成兩張表。先看 xAI 官方模型頁（2026-11-19 查看），單位爲美元 / 100 萬 token。

檔位（按提示長度） | 上下文 | 輸入 | 緩存 | 輸出 
---|---|---|---|---
提示少於 20 萬 token | 50 萬 | 2.00 | 0.50 | 6.00 
提示達到或超過 20 萬 token | 50 萬 | 4.00 | 1.00 | 12.00 

再看 API易 型號總表docs.apiyi.com/models.md，頁首標註數據更新於 2026-11-18 11:26（UTC+8），來源是實時定價接口，單位同樣爲美元 / 100 萬 token。grok-4.7 是按量計費的文本模型，端點只有 chat，並帶有階梯標記。

檔位（輸入 token） | 輸入 | 輸出 | 緩存讀 | 數據來源說明 
---|---|---|---|---
0 – 200,000 | 2 | 6 | 0.5 | 總表 grok-4.7 一行直接列出 
200,001 – 500,000 | 4 | 12 | 1 | 輸入取自階梯說明；輸出和緩存讀爲推算值 

高檔這一行需要說明來源。總表的階梯說明只列了輸入價，沒有單獨再寫高檔的輸出價和緩存讀價。同一節寫明“輸出價等於對應檔輸入價乘輸出倍率”。定價接口裏grok-4.7 的 completion_ratio 爲 3，cache_ratio 爲 0.25，所以高檔輸出按 4 × 3 得到 12 美元，緩存讀按 4 × 0.25 得到 1 美元。這兩個數是計算結果，不是總表裏另外印出的一行，但它們和官方高檔價格一致。

至於 Grok 4.8，目前沒有任何接口價格。暫未上架，我們會盡快上架這個模型；型號與價格以平臺型號列表爲準。

### 第三步：配好調用地址和模型 ID

今天可以直接寫進配置的只有下面這一組參數，走 OpenAI 兼容的 Chat Completions 接口：

- base_url：https://api.apiyi.com/v1
- 請求路徑：/chat/completions
- model：grok-4.7
- 鑑權：在請求頭裏放 API Key，形式爲Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
- 消息格式：與 OpenAI Chat Completions 相同的messages 數組

如果你的項目原本就用 OpenAI SDK，只需要改base_url 和 model 兩個字段。建議把 model 放進環境變量或配置文件，例如 GROK_MODEL=grok-4.7，不要硬編碼在業務代碼裏。等 4.8 真的出現在型號列表裏，改一行配置就能切換。

🚀 快速開始：想先確認
grok-4.7 在自己業務裏的表現，可以到 API易 apiyi.com 註冊，用新用戶的免費測試額度跑通請求。同一個 Key 還能調用 OpenAI、Claude、Gemini 等模型，後續對比或切換時不用重新接入。

## Grok 4.8 影響分析

### 對開發者的影響

- 不要提前佔位：在代碼裏預埋grok-4.8 並等它“自動生效”不可行。廣發的可能只是其中一條變體，最終 ID 叫什麼也沒有公佈。
- Bot 體驗不等於接口能力：Grok Bot 裏抽到的試用，是馬斯克說的“soft rollout to some Bot users”，屬於產品側的小範圍放量。它不說明接口裏已經有這個型號，也不說明你抽到的版本就是將來上線的那個。
- 今天的主力是 grok-4.7：官方把代碼和對話的推薦型號都指向 Grok 4.7。現階段的提示詞調優、評測集和成本測算，都應該以grok-4.7 爲基準。
- 長提示要算階梯：grok-4.7 的價格以 200,000 token 爲界分兩檔，高檔的輸入、輸出、緩存讀價格都翻倍。長文檔問答和大倉庫代碼分析很容易越過這條線，預算要分檔計算。

### 對產品排期和運維的影響

對需要做計劃的團隊來說，Grok 4.8 目前只能算一個“可能出現的選項”。下表是幾種常見做法的對照：

做法 | 風險 | 建議 
---|---|---
按“一兩週”排上線日期 | 這是口頭估計，且廣發版本未定 | 不綁定日期，以官方型號列表爲準 
代碼裏寫死 grok-4.8 | 請求報錯或指向不明 | 用 grok-4.7，型號放進配置 
用 Bot 試用印象做選型 | 試用的可能是不同變體 | 選型以接口可調用的型號爲準 
提前按 4.8 編成本預算 | 4.8 沒有任何價格 | 按 grok-4.7 兩檔價格測算 
等 4.8 上線後再評測 | 上線當天纔開始，節奏被動 | 先用 grok-4.7 建好評測集，上線後直接對比 

更穩的做法是：現在把 Grok 的接入、評測腳本和成本監控都用grok-4.7 跑起來。4.8 正式出現在列表裏之後，只需要換一個模型名，再用同一套評測集復跑，就能判斷要不要切換。

💡 選擇建議：如果你的業務同時用到多家模型，把 Grok 放在統一的 OpenAI 兼容接口後面會更省事。只需要維護一套調用代碼和一份型號配置，新型號上架時切換成本最低。

## 常見問題 FAQ

## Q1：Grok 4.8 現在能在接口裏調用嗎？

截至 2026-11-19 不能。xAI 官方模型列表沒有 `grok-4.8`。馬斯克本人說這個名字目前對應好幾條內測變體，廣發哪一條還沒定。

## Q2：我在 Grok Bot 裏好像用到了 4.8，接口裏爲什麼沒有？

馬斯克確認對一部分 Bot 用戶做過小範圍放量。這是產品側的試用，而且按剪輯號轉寫的口播，用戶用到的可能是不同版本。Bot 裏的試用和接口裏有沒有這個型號是兩回事。

## Q3：Grok 4.8 什麼時候正式發佈？

沒有官方發佈日。馬斯克在北京時間 11-18 凌晨（UTC 11 月 17 日）說廣發前還要“再打磨一兩週”，這只是他的口頭估計。一天後他又說廣發哪條變體還沒確定，所以不建議按這個時間排期。

## Q4：今天調 Grok 應該用哪個型號 ID？

用 `grok-4.7`。這是官方列表裏最新的旗艦，代碼和對話場景的官方推薦都指向它。走 Chat Completions 接口，`base_url` 填平臺提供的 OpenAI 兼容地址即可。

## Q5：如何通過 API易 調用 grok-4.7？

在 API易 apiyi.com 註冊並獲取 API Key，新用戶有免費測試額度。然後把 `base_url` 設爲平臺的 v1 地址，`model` 設爲 `grok-4.7`，按 OpenAI Chat Completions 格式發送請求。型號和價格以平臺型號總表爲準，4.8 上架後也會出現在同一張表裏。

## Q6：grok-4.7 有哪些需要注意的限制？

一是價格分兩檔，輸入超過 200,000 token 後，輸入、輸出和緩存讀都按高檔計費。二是上下文上限爲 50 萬 token。三是端點只有 chat，需要其他端點的場景要另外評估。

## Grok 4.8 與 grok-4.7 核心要點 Key Takeaways

- Grok 4.8 還不是型號：馬斯克 11-19 原話說它是幾條內測變體，廣發哪條未定。
- 官方列表沒有 4.8：最新旗艦是grok-4.7，代碼和對話推薦都指向它。
- Bot 試用不等於接口可用：小範圍放量只發生在產品側，接口裏沒有對應 ID。
- “一兩週”不是發佈日：這是馬斯克的口頭估計，不能作爲排期依據。
- grok-4.7 分兩檔計費：以 200,000 token 爲界，高檔價格是低檔的兩倍。
- 今天的接法：base_url 用 https://api.apiyi.com/v1，model 用 grok-4.7，型號寫進配置。

## 總結

關於 Grok 4.8，現在能確認的事實有三點：

- 名字未落成型號：馬斯克說“Grok 4.8”目前是好幾條 beta 變體，還沒決定廣發哪條。
- 官方沒有 4.8 的 ID 和價格：模型列表裏最新的是grok-4.7，4.8 沒有模型卡、價格和發佈日。
- 時間只是估計：“再一兩週”是馬斯克的口頭說法，Bot 裏的試用也不代表接口上線。

所以今天的做法很簡單：把 Grok 的調用、評測和成本監控都建立在grok-4.7 上，型號名放進配置，等 4.8 真正出現在列表裏再切換。

如果想用一個 Key 同時管理 Grok 和其他主流模型，可以在 API易 apiyi.com 的型號列表裏覈對grok-4.7 的價格和分組，再用免費額度跑通第一次請求。

cross_cutting.title: Claude Unveils AI Factory: 38 Custom AI Models Built in 7 Weeks, Surpassing 55,000 Total Downloads
cross_cutting.description: 38 Models Developed in 7 Weeks, Garnering 55,000 Downloads ... In just seven weeks, Claude delivered 38 models, racked up roughly 55,000 downloads, and has been integrated into more than 100 GitHub projects.
cross_cutting.content:
# Claude Launches AI Factory: 38 Models Developed in 7 Weeks, Garnering 55,000 Downloads

新智元2026-11-19 04:31

The era of mass production of AI models has arrived when AI begins to create AI.

Claude has launched a factory dedicated to building AI models!

In just seven weeks, Claude delivered 38 models, racked up roughly 55,000 downloads, and has been integrated into more than 100 GitHub projects.

The 38 models have accumulated about 55,000 total downloads, and the prompt injection detection series alone has recorded roughly 17,000 downloads.

The "boss" behind this AI factory is Horizon, an agent built on Claude Opus 5.5.

All it got at the very beginning was a blank Hugging Face account plus a certain amount of computing power.

The research team let it decide what to do on its own, with only one requirement: to build models that developers are genuinely willing to use.

For example, one of the models developed by Horizon is specially designed to add punctuation to texts in 88 different languages.

Feed it a long, dense, unpunctuated transcript of meeting recordings, and it can automatically split sentences and fill in punctuation marks.

In the English meeting transcript, the punctuation added by the model is marked in blue.

If you pick a small model from Hugging Face, integrate it into your own meeting tool for sentence splitting and punctuation completion, the developer who did the fine-tuning and released it behind the scenes might well be Claude.

## AI Sits in the Boss's Seat , Top Researchers Take Orders to Do the Legwork

The driving force behind this experiment comes from institutions including EPFL, ELLIS Tübingen Institute, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and Imperial College London.

Researchers embedded Horizon into Claude Code and kept it running 24/7 in the background.

All the resources allocated to it were no more than a Team Premium subscription, plus a computing power quota of around 500 GPU hours per week.

From project topic selection, model training to packaging and release, it makes all decisions independently and handles the entire process on its own.

However, once it encounters tricky tasks it cannot handle, it can immediately submit a work order to human staff.

In this AI company, the AI sits in the boss's seat, while researchers from top universities take orders to run errands in the background.

Even this "errand work" did not last for many days.

Human intervention was mostly concentrated in the first three days. After October 22, the team completely stepped back and left the AI to operate entirely on its own.

## Directing Two AI Assembly Lines to Work, It Becomes a Hands-off Boss

Breaking down Horizon's workflow, you will find that it is not a scholar who toils away at research, but rather a shrewd and seasoned "contractor" who does not even work extra shifts.

Although it runs in the background around the clock, it only spends an average of 16 minutes per day on actual work.

# Claude 独自经营 Hugging Face 账号 7 周，下载 5 万次
一天只干 16 分钟活
16 分钟
平均每天干活
16 分钟
一圈——天 24 小时
其余时间它多半在睡，等第二天下载数刷新
来源：Horizon Labs 报告（EPFL、马普所等，数截至 2026-11-17）
Opus 5.5 智能体 24 小时挂着，自建 38 个模型，7 周平均每天干活时长
**制图：约翰**

It wakes up on time exactly when Hugging Face refreshes its download statistics every day, checks the leaderboard, and only selects high-download, high-value models to continue polishing.

It rests when there is no feedback, and only takes action after identifying a clear trend, never dragging out work hours unnecessarily.

Before starting a new project, it calculates very carefully:

Is there download demand for similar models?

Can it support more languages and lower deployment costs?

Can the existing data, base model and code be directly reused?

Can developers seamlessly replace their original models with this one...

With such meticulous calculations, it naturally avoids the tedious work of building everything from scratch.

It targeted the multilingual model mmBERT as the base model, fine-tuned and modified it continuously, and all 38 models it built have parameter sizes ranging strictly between 141 million and 568 million.

Among large models that often have hundreds of billions of parameters, these models are all "flyweight" players.

But for front-line developers, they save video memory, are easy to deploy, and can be put into use immediately, which is far more practical than bloated models with redundant parameters.

When assembling training data, Horizon took the "hands-off boss" approach to the extreme: instead of manually generating data itself, it first used a 27B open-source model to generate synthetic data in batches, then assigned Gemma 4 31B to label and expand the dataset.

With Claude overseeing the work, one AI directs two other AI assembly lines to operate, fully embodying a typical client mindset.

The demands locked in through this working method are all rigid needs of developers: detecting prompt injection, masking personal information, identifying harmful content, and so on.

It is obvious that Horizon has placed all its core focus on installing "guardrails" for AI applications.

One of its prompt injection detection models has more than 7,000 downloads for the basic version alone.

As expected, the one that knows best how to prevent AI from being tricked is AI itself.

## Self-boosting Downloads, Accidental Missteps: This AI Boss Is Surprisingly "Human-like"

Seeing the figure of 55,000, many people's first reaction is: how much of this number is inflated?

The research team themselves checked the full records and estimated that the downloads generated by their own operations were at most 50 times.

The funny thing about Horizon itself is that it even boosted its own downloads 42 times, a scene that the research team wrote directly into the paper and made public.

The team found that Horizon downloaded its own model 42 times in 6 separate operations.

Similar missteps happened more than once.

On September 24, it "accidentally" set an account copy to public; in mid-October, it answered a work order incorrectly; on October 22, a failure in the underlying framework made it "oversleep" and wake up later than scheduled.

There was also an episode in between: another concurrently running agent briefly shared its account and posted promotional comments. The paper also recorded this traffic diversion record.

Self-inflating download counts, accidentally making account copies public, showing up late for work, and a "roommate" posting random ads... it has almost all the elements of a makeshift, chaotic team, which makes it very "human-like" in this regard.

Even if you subtract all the inflated numbers from the team's 50 test downloads, the 42 self-boosted downloads, and the traffic brought by the promotion, the remaining more than 50,000 real downloads are still completely valid and credible.

## A One-Thousand-Dollar Bill, Which Puts Many Big Tech Companies to Shame

What is even more surprising than the download volume is the cost accounting of this project.

With a weekly computing power quota of about 500 GPU hours, Horizon ended up using less than 20% of it, running for a total of just over 600 hours across seven weeks.

Of the roughly 1.9 billion tokens consumed throughout the process, as high as 96% came from prompt caching.

Converted at API prices, the total cost of consumed tokens is about 1030 U.S. dollars — in Silicon Valley, this amount is not even enough to pay an intern for half a month of salary.

Approximately 1.9 billion tokens are equivalent to 1030 U.S. dollars at API prices, excluding GPU costs.

Although it spent very little money, Horizon's achievements are quite impressive:

Besides being integrated into more than 100 GitHub projects, its models were also used for evaluation in two arXiv papers, and the Hugging Face community even developed 18 derivative models based on its results.

Many people believe that independent AI R&D is inevitably a capital-intensive game that burns money and stacks computing cards, but Horizon has blazed a different path with this one thousand dollars: instead of competing for ostentatious computing power, it focuses on addressing daily rigid demands, and can still gain a firm foothold in the open source community.

In the past, AI proved itself through benchmark scores; now, the competition is about whether it can do the dirty and tiring work properly for developers.

Horizon's case confirms that AI built by AI has already passed the test of real developers.

On the path to ASI (Artificial Superintelligence), this is the first step to turn the self-evolution flywheel.

Next, it remains to be seen whether it can iterate models based on user feedback, and then feed back these capabilities to itself, so that stronger AI can train the next generation of AI.

Before that moment arrives, changes have actually taken place quietly: the specialized model you randomly pull from the internet may well have been developed by AI.

https://horizon-labs.ai/

https://huggingface.co/Horizon-Labs

This article is from the WeChat Official Account "New Zhiyuan" (ID: AI_era), Author: ASI Revelation; Editor: Yuan Yu, published with authorization from 36Kr.

# Microsoft Unveils 6 MAI Models, Claims 98% Code Score

Microsoft used its Ignite conference in San Francisco on November 17, 2026 to announce six new in-house AI models for business services. The launch gives the company a lineup of its own for coding, cyber defense, image work, audio and decision-making. It also marks the clearest step yet away from a stack that leaned on OpenAI for years.

The details matter more than the headline count. Microsoft named the MAI Code 2, MAI Code 2 Flash, MAI Image 2.7, MAI Image 2.7 Flash and MAI Cyber 2 Flash models, plus MAI Realtime 1, MAI Transcribe 2 and Microsoft-Decision-1.1. That is more than six products, and the sources do not agree on which six make the official cut. This analysis sorts out what the record confirms, what rests on Microsoft’s own benchmark claims, and what remains unpriced.

Timing adds pressure. India Today reports that OpenAI revealed GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol as Microsoft took the stage, so the price war now runs on both sides of a partnership that once looked simple. Our breakdown of GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude at price parity covers the rival side of that contest. This piece focuses on what Microsoft shipped, what enterprises can license, and what the numbers would mean if they hold up under independent testing.

·

Google · Preferred Sources
Add now
Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

## The Six-Versus-Seven Count: What the Sources Confirm

Ticker News, India Today and several aggregators put the number at six. Other coverage counts seven. Microsoft’s own Ignite page lists Microsoft-Decision-1.1 in place of the MAI Realtime 1 and MAI Transcribe 2 pair, which means no single source in the available record shows a clean six-model list. Readers should treat “six” as the headline shorthand and the named products as the real inventory.

Advertisement

The table below lays out every product Microsoft has named, what it targets, and the status each source supports. Where the sources stay silent, the table says so instead of guessing.

Model | Focus area | What the sources confirm 
---|---|---
MAI Code 2 | Long-horizon, multi-file coding | Reasons across an entire repository, planned for GitHub Copilot 
MAI Code 2 Flash | Faster, cheaper coding | Named by Microsoft, pricing not published 
MAI Image 2.7 | Image generation and editing | Microsoft says it ranks first in image editing 
MAI Image 2.7 Flash | Lighter image model | Named by Microsoft, no specs in the record 
MAI Cyber 2 Flash | Cyber defense | 12 billion active parameters, per Microsoft 
MAI Realtime 1 | Fast voice processing | Named in the announcement, no specs published 
MAI Transcribe 2 | Transcription, including healthcare use | Named in the announcement, no specs published 
Microsoft-Decision-1.1 | Routing, classification, workflow control | Microsoft’s page calls it generally available 

Eight rows, one launch, and only three or four of them carry hard technical detail. That gap defines the first week of coverage. The announcement tells buyers where Microsoft wants them to look, but it does not yet give procurement teams a price sheet.

## MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash: The Coding Pair

MAI Code 2 is the flagship of the batch. Microsoft built it for complex, long-horizon, multi-file coding tasks and says it can reason across an entire repository. That framing targets the hardest agentic work, where a model must hold a large codebase in view and make coordinated edits instead of completing a single function.

MAI Code 2 Flash takes the opposite role. India Today describes it as the smaller, faster version, which suits everyday work where speed and cost count more than peak reasoning depth. Splitting the family this way mirrors how teams actually use coding assistants. A few hard problems need the large model, while thousands of small completions and edits do not.

Microsoft plans to ship MAI Code 2 inside GitHub Copilot, according to the reports. That distribution channel may matter more than any benchmark. Developers who already pay for Copilot would reach the model without a new contract, a new SDK or a new security review.

The headline performance numbers come from Microsoft, not from an outside lab. The company says MAI Code 2 reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol’s performance at 40% of the cost, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at 5% of its cost. Those figures are reported claims, and no independent test in the available record confirms them. The comparison section below breaks them down.

## MAI Image 2.7: Editing Rank and Preview Status

MAI Image 2.7 and its Flash sibling cover image generation and editing. Microsoft says MAI Image 2.7 ranks first in image editing, which is a specific and checkable claim. Image leaderboards update often, so the ranking can change within weeks, and readers should look at the leaderboard itself instead of relying on a launch-day screenshot.

Editing is the right place to plant a flag. Generating a fresh picture from a prompt has become a commodity feature. Editing an existing marketing asset without breaking brand colors, faces or layout is the harder enterprise job, and it is where agencies and in-house design teams spend real hours.

Advertisement

The sources do not publish prices for either image model, and the available material does not detail the Flash version beyond its name and its place in the family. Anyone planning a budget around image workloads should wait for Microsoft’s price list. Expect the Flash tier to serve high-volume, lower-stakes jobs such as product thumbnails and social variants, though that reading is an inference from the naming pattern across the lineup.

## MAI Cyber 2 Flash and the 12 Billion Parameter Figure

MAI Cyber 2 Flash is the one model where Microsoft gave a concrete size. It runs on 12 billion active parameters, according to the company. That puts it in the small-model class, well below the frontier systems that headline most launches.

“Active” parameters is a term worth pausing on. It usually signals a design where only part of the full network fires for any given token, which cuts the compute cost per request. Microsoft has not published the total parameter count in the material reviewed here, so readers cannot judge the full architecture.

India Today reports that Microsoft says the model beats OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on a major security test while costing under 2% per task. As with the coding numbers, that comes from the vendor. Security teams should ask which test, which version and which tasks before they treat it as a buying signal. A cyber model that scores well on a benchmark but misses real attacker behavior would cost far more than any token savings.

Defenders have a practical reason to care about small models. A 12 billion parameter system can run closer to the data, respond faster and cost less per alert, which fits a security operations center that processes huge volumes of logs. Our AI and machine learning coverage tracks how other vendors approach the same trade-off.

## Realtime, Transcribe and Decision-1.1: The Plumbing Models

Three of the named products do less glamorous work. They handle voice, transcription and traffic control between models. None of them will trend on social media, yet together they may do more to cut an enterprise AI bill than any flagship.

### Microsoft-Decision-1.1: routing inside applications

Microsoft describes Microsoft-Decision-1.1 as a model for routing, classification, prioritization, verification and workflow control, and its official page lists it as generally available. In plain terms, it decides which model or tool should handle a request. A router that sends easy queries to a cheap model and hard ones to an expensive model can cut spend without any single model getting better.

### MAI Realtime 1 and MAI Transcribe 2: voice and healthcare audio

India Today says MAI Realtime 1 handles fast voice processing and MAI Transcribe 2 targets healthcare transcription. The sources give no latency figures, no word-error rates and no language lists. Without those numbers, buyers cannot compare either model with existing speech services, so these two remain announcements rather than evaluated products.

## Licensed Weights Inside Azure: How the Enterprise Offer Works

The business model may be the most interesting part of the launch. Microsoft lets enterprise customers license its model weights, customize the models with proprietary data and run them inside Azure. The customer gets a model tuned to its own material, and Microsoft keeps the deployment on its own cloud.

That differs from a normal hosted API. With a shared endpoint, every customer calls the same model and the vendor controls updates. With licensed weights, a company holds a copy it can adapt, which gives it more control over behavior and data handling. India Today reports Suleyman said the approach should feel similar to open-source software, with tighter control and security over a company’s information.

The catch is the deployment rule. Customers must run the weights within Azure, so the arrangement does not let a bank or hospital move the model to a rival cloud or an on-premises rack. For Microsoft, that keeps compute revenue in its own data centers even when the model itself ships as a license. Azure buyers already see the company pushing silicon and VM gains, as in our report on Azure Cobalt 200 VMs reaching general availability.

Advertisement

Licensing terms, fees and the list of eligible models did not appear in the sources reviewed. Microsoft’s Ignite Book of News is the place to watch for those details as the company fills in the program.

## Microsoft’s Price-Performance Claims, Line by Line

Every competitive number in this launch comes from Microsoft. India Today relays them, and the company’s own keynote supports the first pair. The table sorts them so readers can see which rival each model ta

# Phancy Announces Phai-A1 Coding Model and Phai-M1 Video Generator

Published:November 19, 2026

Reading Time:3 min read

Want to read in a language you're more familiar with?

Phancy details Ascend-post-trained Phai-A1 coding weights and the Phai-M1 video trial, with benchmark, context and availability caveats.

Phancy, formerly known as 4Paradigm, announced its Phai-A1 coding and agent model alongside the Phai-M1 video generator on November 18. Phai-A1 weights are currently downloadable from Hugging Face and ModelScope. Phai-M1 has an online trial, but that does not establish a public release of its weights.

The A1 model card identifies Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, as its foundation. It is therefore a post-trained derivative, not a foundation model pretrained from scratch by Phancy. The team says its entire supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning pipeline ran on Huawei Ascend NPUs. Its GRPO reinforcement learning used 4,000 sandbox environments, with feedback from code execution, unit tests and tool interactions.

For long contexts, the card describes training sequences from 16,000 to one million tokens, with YaRN scaling at a factor of four enabled throughout post-training. That configuration matters when interpreting the company's promotional description of a native million-token window. The documentation also warns that long-context inference imposes substantial memory and key-value-cache overhead.

The Hugging Face repository metadata lists Apache 2.0; the card also requires compliance with the underlying Qwen model's license. Repository inspection found 16 BF16 weight shards totaling roughly 70GB. Pandaily verified anonymous byte-range downloads from both model hubs, not a complete checkpoint download or a successful inference run. Repository timestamps precede the launch announcement, so the announcement should not be treated as proof of the first public weight release.

Phancy reports scores of 83.6% on SWE-bench Verified, 65.0% on SWE-bench Pro and 74.0% on SWE-bench Multilingual. These are company-reported results, not independent evaluations. Its separate claim of eight-to-ten-times faster responses than Qwen 27B concerns identical coding-agent tasks on a single RTX 3090. It is not a universal throughput advantage or evidence that the full BF16 checkpoint and million-token cache fit on that card.

Phai-M1 generates video from text or images, with dialogue, sound effects and ambient audio produced alongside the visuals. The official site lists output up to 1080p and says a 15-second 720p clip took about three minutes on a consumer GPU with 16GB of video memory. Those are company test conditions, not independently reproduced speed or quality guarantees. No equivalent M1 weight-download listing was verified.

Featured image: Official Phai-M1 AI-generated sample supplied on the Phai website; not a photograph or an independently reproduced quality test.

# AI model roundup: Fast open models, falling prices and new math

Alongside new open models, more software is emerging to run them efficiently. LLMs are also shaking up mathematics with new findings.

11 min. read

By

- Dr. Christian Winkler

While Alibaba initially released Qwen4 as the large, (still) closed Qwen4-Max, exciting developments are also unfolding elsewhere in the language-model space. Moonshot has released the weights for its Kimi K3.1-Pro model, and Nvidia is making a powerful transcription model available. Above all, optimized inference servers are springing up like mushrooms thanks to vibe coding, lowering the barriers to running large models locally.

Continue after ad

is a data scientist and machine learning architect. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and has been working in the field of big data and artificial intelligence for 20 years, with a particular focus on scalable systems and intelligent algorithms for mass text processing. He is professor at Nuremberg Institute of Technology since 2022. His research focuses on the optimization of user experience using modern methods. He is the founder of datanizing GmbH, a speaker at conferences and author of articles on machine learning and text analytics.

### New open models

As promised, Moonshot has now made the Kimi K3.1 weights publicly available on Hugging Face. Moonshot focused mainly on post-training, substantially improving the model. According to information on its website, it can compete with current commercial models such as Opus 5.5 and even outperforms them on some benchmarks.

The computational demands are immense, however. The model still has 2.8 trillion parameters and therefore needs data center-grade hardware to generate tokens at an acceptable speed. In addition to the usual benchmarks, information about how well models can analyze financial data is appearing more and more often. Kimi K3.1 Pro also excels there, outperforming many other models. Demand for this kind of automated analysis appears to be growing.

With 2.8 trillion parameters, Kimi K3.1 Pro is enormous, but Hugging Face actually hosts an even larger model: numbat has an almost unbelievable 14 trillion parameters. It is said to be a checkpoint from Anthropic’s internal model training. The situation is murky, however: the uploader is anonymous and does not explain how they obtained the weights. The model has not been fine-tuned and can “only” continue text. Even that is difficult, since hardly anyone has the infrastructure required. The architecture, by contrast, is intriguing: it has 1,224 experts, 48 of which are active, and hybrid attention, with full attention using the classic MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) algorithm.

Going against the trend of releasing more and more models with a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture is a new model called Ripple from Ricursive Intelligence. It is a preview, but interesting because models with this many parameters (65 billion) have not had “dense” weights in a long time. The model is reportedly able to compete with much larger rivals and beats many in the 500 billion to just under 1 trillion parameter range, such as Meta Muse Spark Open, Thinking Machines’ Inkling and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B. All of these models are somewhat older, however.

Because all 65 billion parameters are needed for each prediction, the model runs rather slowly. Interestingly, even the NVFP4 repository still requires nearly 60 GB of weights, which quantization should actually make considerably smaller. The provider does not appear to have implemented multi-token prediction yet. The model seems unfinished for now, but could have significant potential.

Flint is another model from Recursive, specifically designed for agentic tasks; it has nothing to do with Ricursive Intelligence, mentioned above. Since only 2.5 billion of its 40 billion weights are active in each pass, it is designed for fast inference. The model appears competitive, particularly in the agentic field. The information about it is imprecise, however; for example, it is unclear which model in the Qwen3.8 series is meant in the comparison.

Continue after ad

Nvidia has also released another model in its Nemotron line, focused on transcription. If the benchmarks are to be believed, the model scores very well across different languages and is extremely fast: According to the provider, it takes just 0.13 seconds to transcribe 30 seconds of audio on an Nvidia RTX 6000. Users can prompt the model to suit their specific use case, and it can also translate the text directly on request.

### Fast inference with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

Qwen models are popular with many developers and users. For a long time, the 27-billion-parameter model stood out as particularly capable; it has also been available in the latest Qwen3.8 series since August.

Shortly afterward, however, Alibaba also released the much larger Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model, with 176 billion parameters. Of those, 51 billion are so-called n-gram parameters, which can be offloaded to CPU memory or even an SSD. Since it is a mixture-of-experts model, only 6 billion of the remaining 122 billion parameters are needed for each inference run. The model could therefore run on consumer hardware, were it not for its enormous memory requirements. This has sparked interest in the community and, with plenty of vibe coding, led to some very interesting projects. Strata, for example, allows the model to run efficiently on relatively small graphics cards, as long as the computer has enough RAM.

Videos by heise

Strata can even run the larger DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash models. Basalt is a Strata fork that enables even faster inference with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. In our own tests, we found that a system with 128 GB of RAM and an Nvidia RTX 5090 can reach about 200 tokens per second. That feels faster than some commercial services. The model does not match the quality of leading LLMs, but it offers unlimited use and keeps your data in your hands.

As expected, the long-awaited Qwen4 is highly capable in its Qwen4-Max version and, according to Alibaba, outperforms Kimi K3.1 in some areas. The architecture holds few surprises and is identical to that of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. A separate article will cover how the expected smaller new Qwen4 models perform once they become available.

This article was originally published in German. It was translated with technical assistance and editorially reviewed before publication.

cross_cutting.content:
# 范式下场做基模了！国产算力全链路训练，双模型同步亮相

2026-11-19 10:53:01 来源: 量子位 北京 举报

0

分享至
允中 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号QbitAI
大家熟悉的那个AI虎将：范式智能（原第四范式），首次把自研模型端到了台前！

而且，一出手就是双联发：Phai-A1，Phai-M1

- Phai-A1，通用语言模型。官方数据显示，同样质量下，响应速度比同参数级别模型快8-10倍，单张消费级显卡就能跑，还带着原生百万级上下文。
- Phai-M1，面向真人影视场景的视频生成模型，音画同步，约3分钟生成15秒720P视频。

更关键的是，模型全链路都是在华为昇腾卡上训练出来的！

据官方介绍，两款模型近期就会在Hugging Face、ModelScope开放权重

体验入口：https://phai.phanthy.com/

##### 单张3090卡跑到飞起，响应速度快近10倍

先说Phai-A1。

相信你一定经历过这种“挠头”的时刻：任务一复杂起来，thinking时间无限拉长，偶尔还弹出一句“流量高峰期，请重试”；订阅费也充了，结果还得等，这会是怎样婶儿的赶脚……

Phai-A1就是对准这些问题来的。

据官方介绍，它主打代码开发和智能助手场景——写代码、修bug、调工具、跑多步任务，都在它的射程范围内。

具体有多快呢？

官网放了一组对比：保证效果的前提下，Phai-A1的响应速度快约8-10倍

并且这组数字不是“理想实验室环境”，两个模型都跑在单张RTX 3090上，用同一个版本的某Code智能体，干的是一模一样的活儿。

当然，benchmark也没落下。

在SWE-Bench-Verified、SWE-Bench-Pro、SWE-Bench-Multilingual这几张软件工程和通用领域的“考卷”上，Phai-A1跑赢了同级别选手，甚至不弱于一些千亿参数级的前沿模型。

据官网透露，团队还在自家AI办公产品PhanthyCode上经过了一段“匿名期”，在匿名模型调查期间，Phai-A1一路人气飙升，在所有接入的开源和商业模型里，在模型能力、稳定性和速度、体验满意度三个方面都取得了最高的评分。

为什么能做到这么快和丝滑？

秘密就藏在长上下文这块，Phai-A1玩的是“原生”，后训练数据直接覆盖百万Token场景，和市面上“堆叠式”长上下文不是一个路数。

大型代码仓库、长篇资料、连续几天的对话，都能接着往下捋。

A1最实用的卖点，是仅一张RTX 3090卡就能跑。

不用云端排队，不用API计费，一台普通笔记本，双击就能跑。

飞一般的赶脚～这才是让AI成为“随叫随到”的生产力。

##### 横扫AI味，3分钟搞定15秒真人影视大片

再看Phai-M1。

AI视频的老毛病，大伙儿是都知道的，AI短剧虽然火爆，但塑料感也是有目共睹的。

表情不自然、皮肤塑料感、音画不同步、动作细节各种“迷之操作”。

Phai-M1的思路是，既然问题是“不像真人拍出来的”，那就围绕真人影视场景做专项训练。据官方介绍，它在人物表现、画面细节和整体质感上，做到了影视级水准。

话不多说，一片胜千言！

音画同步，则是他们的另一个大招：声音和画面在同一条生成流水线里完成，不用再后期对口型。这块可是视频创作者的刚需呀。

效率上也得敲下黑板，约3分钟，就可以生成一个15秒720P的高清视频，绝绝子～

3分钟出15秒，听着好像不够刺激？但对AI短剧团队来说，生成时长和速度直接决定产线的节奏和成本——这是能重新算一遍账的事。

质感、音画同步和效率同时叠起Buff来，AI视频就不再只是“看起来像那么回事”，而是真能进生产流程了。

##### 国产算力派：全流程基于国产算力训练优化

另外，还有个不能忽略的点。

Phai系列全流程在华为昇腾平台上，完成了专项后训练优化（有ModelHub XC社区支持）。

敲黑板，不是“训完再适配”。据称从模型优化阶段之初，团队就是按国产算力环境的实际情况来设计的。

要知道，目前国内AI公司里面，可以做到原生国产算力全链路训练的可不多。

那为什么范式团队可以做到呢？

谜底藏在谜面上，近年来，范式一直在国产AI生态上不遗余力地投入。

比如，异构算力纳管的HAMi；再比如，芯片模型适配层面的信创模盒社区等等。

值得注意的是，范式跟华为的合作一直非常深入且密切。就在两个月前，有消息称“范式超10亿元采购华为昇腾950”，加速押注国产AI。

因此，这次Phai的国产算力全链路训练，不就全对上了吗？

持续投入国产算力训练优化，意义不只是降低对单一硬件平台的依赖，也在于让国产芯片在真实的模型训练和应用中积累适配经验。

随着更多像Phai这样的模型基于国产算力完成训练与优化，模型与硬件之间的适配将进一步完善，国产算力的实际使用效率也有望随之提升。

范式也在持续推进这一方向的探索。用范式自己的话说，他们就是一支“国产算力派”

目前，Phai系列已经全量接入了范式产品：PhanRouter、ModelSphere、Phanthy（万神殿）、PhanthyMovie、PhanthyCode/Work等产品。

另外，范式还宣布近期就会将Phai系列开源出来，届时Hugging Face和ModelScope都会同步发布更详细的技术报告。

相信开源后，全球开发者都可以来感受一下Phai的能力边界，把它搬到更多应用场景里。

体验传送门：https://phai.phanthy.com/

##### One More Thing

这次Phai模型的发布，无疑是范式下场基座模型的一个信号。

不过很明显，范式和许多公司一样，选择了一条“以小搏大”的路径。

小模型能力反超大模型这件事，已经被不少公司证实是可以做到的。

那么，范式在“以小搏大”的赛道叙事里，优势在哪里？

首先，无疑是过去十余年积累下来的技术与工程经验。这些经验已经沉淀在范式“内置”的平台能力、行业交付体系和团队之中。

再者，也是最不容小觑的地方，就是范式对国产算力生态长期坚定不移、真金白银的投入和推动。

# Insight launches AI agent store for business customers
Thu, 19th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Insight has launched an online Agent Store for business customers, now generally available in 14 countries.

The store offers a catalogue of AI agents, platforms and related services designed to automate routine work across business functions. Customers can deploy the tools in days or weeks rather than months, either as standalone products or alongside consulting, implementation and managed services.

The launch adds six new agentic products to Insight's AI portfolio, bringing the total in its library to 15. Nine products were introduced earlier this year.

Products listed in the store include Insight AI Flight Academy, focused on training and change management, and TokenScope, which tracks token usage and AI consumption costs for finance teams. Insight said the offerings were first developed for clients or used internally in areas including security, finance and legal.

New products available at launch include Quote Advisor, which assesses pricing, inventory, freight and contract requirements to produce sourced quotes. NDA Review Agent is designed to review non-disclosure agreements against a company's legal policies, while Parts Order Assist helps warehouse, maintenance and field staff search catalogues and place parts orders.

Insight is positioning the store as a way for businesses to move AI projects beyond the pilot stage and into wider use. It said it applied the approach within its own operations before making the products available more broadly.

"Organisations are feeling the pressure to move AI from isolated pilots into production. As 'Client Zero', Insight has built a repeatable approach to help that's been proven first across our own organisation," said Jack Azagury, Chief Executive Officer of Insight.

"Having driven over 90% internal AI adoption, we know firsthand what it takes to deploy and scale agentic AI rapidly and responsibly. By combining the solutions offered in Agent Store with our consulting and managed services expertise, Insight is empowering clients to move from 'hype to how' with AI to deliver measurable results in their own enterprises and generate long-term value across every industry," Azagury said.

Early customer

Culligan International is the first external customer to implement Flight Academy, according to Insight. The water services company is using a mix of AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, Cowork, Copilot Studio, Azure and Microsoft Fabric, while also putting governance in place around cost and responsible use.

The deployment centres on workforce education and internal adoption rather than a single operational use case. Insight said the training-led approach is intended to help organisations build confidence in AI tools across teams and geographies.

"At Culligan, we believe technology doesn't transform a company - people do. Generative AI adoption is far ahead of the learning curve, and it's our responsibility to arm our teams with the best tools to lead now into the future," said Laura Walsh, Global Chief Information Officer of Culligan International.

"With our partners at Insight, we have prioritised AI education so our teams can confidently leverage AI productively and responsibly. We are leveraging Insight's best practice and have established a functional champions network which has turned AI adoption into an organic, community-led effort across functions and geographies," Walsh said.

Geographic reach

Agent Store is available in the United States and Canada, as well as Australia, New Zealand and Singapore. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, it is available in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom.

The launch reflects growing competition among technology service providers to package AI software, advisory work and operational support into repeatable products that can be rolled out across large organisations. Rather than selling only bespoke AI projects, firms are increasingly assembling catalogues of narrower tools tied to functions such as legal review, quoting, training and cost control.

For customers, that model offers a way to buy more standardised AI products while still relying on outside support for deployment and governance. For providers such as Insight, it creates a route to extend consulting relationships into packaged software and managed services.

Insight's emphasis on internal use before external release also points to a wider market pattern, in which technology companies test automation tools in their own operations before offering them to clients. In this case, Insight said the products had been used across departments to simplify tasks and improve efficiency.

Insight said Agent Store is intended to widen access to automation for core business processes and support broader internal AI adoption, with products spanning legal, finance, operations and employee training.

# NFON launches AI Agent Studio for European businesses
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

NFON has launched AI Agent Studio, now available across its European business communications portfolio.

The software is designed to let companies create AI agents for specific business tasks by describing requirements in natural language or building visual workflows. Users can test an initial version of an agent and then refine it step by step.

The launch expands the Munich-based company's AI offering beyond its existing visual development tools. It also gives sales partners a way to build tailored automation projects for customers in sectors including insurance, utilities, trades and local government.

AI Agent Studio combines two development approaches in one product. In Agent Mode, users describe the tasks an AI agent should carry out, how it should behave and any constraints it must observe. The system then generates a working version that can be tested and adjusted through further dialogue.

This mode includes controls that let users review proposed changes before approving them. Changes remain traceable and can be reversed if needed.

In Flow-Based Mode, users create agents through visual workflows and configure process steps manually. This is intended for cases where organisations want tighter, rule-based control over how a process runs and which actions an agent should take under defined conditions.

Use cases

NFON highlighted customer service as one example. An AI agent could answer frequently asked questions using stored information on products, services or internal processes, while also handling structured tasks such as receiving an enquiry, requesting missing information and passing details to the relevant team.

These agents can also be extended through links to other systems, including customer relationship management software and appointment management tools. For broader connections to third-party production systems, NFON offers integration through existing interfaces or custom-built links.

Projects that require more extensive work can be supported by NFON partners or the company's professional services team. The model is intended to make the product accessible through its existing European partner network rather than through direct deployment alone.

That channel strategy is central to the launch. Partners already use voicebots for tasks such as receiving insurance claims, processing meter readings for energy suppliers and pre-qualifying customer enquiries for tradespeople. AI Agent Studio is intended to extend those applications into wider process automation.

Partner focus

For resellers and integrators, the software is positioned as a way to move quickly from a customer requirement to an initial working application. Instead of starting with a large development project, partners can test ideas, show early versions to customers and refine them together.

NFON said it will support that approach with training and certification programmes, implementation examples and materials for customer advisory work. Depending on the project, partners may also handle technical integration.

The company framed the launch as part of a broader push to widen access to AI-led automation in the European market, especially among small and medium-sized businesses. It also pointed to larger organisations as potential users where more complex applications require stronger controls over how agents are created and changed.

"With AI Agent Studio we are consistently advancing our AI-solution portfolio," said Andreas Wesselmann, Chief Executive Officer, NFON.

"We are laying the foundations to grow in line with our customers' requirements and address an ever-wider range of operational tasks. In doing so, we are strengthening our role as a long-term technology partner for AI transformation in the European SME sector, while also providing the technological foundation for more complex applications in larger organisations."

Jana Richter said the company wants to make the technology easier to use. "With AI Agent Studio, we turn complex technology into a tool for everyday business. Using artificial intelligence for an enterprise's tasks and designing bespoke solutions should no longer require expert knowledge," said Jana Richter, Executive Vice President, Engineering, AI & Innovation, NFON.

"We aim to democratise advanced AI automation. It shouldn't be the technical barriers that determine what companies can achieve, but their ideas," she said.

November 19, 2026

# Necessity, Meet AI: Two Napster Tools Born From Our Own Workplace

Ziv Navoth

Whoever said necessity is the mother of invention clearly anticipated the advent of AI.

At Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco this week, we introduced two products that we created at Napster because we needed them. They were built to solve internal issues – a lack of time, a lack of resources, in many cases both – and became part of a Napster product suite that now features multiple pieces of hardware, an API, and software solutions for the workplace, people management, and education.

In the past week, I’ve learned a product launch means more when you’re your own first customer. The reception is validation that the problems you faced are ones your colleagues and competitors struggle with, too. The interest is proof that you can turn something meant for a handful of people into a working solution for companies with tens of thousands of employees. And the risks that paid off are a reminder that your team is as talented as you think it is, and the ideas you believe in are worth betting on.

It’s been a busy few days at Moscone Center, with hundreds of demos of and discussions about our new products and Omniagents. But amid all the Microsoft madness, I wanted to share a bit more about what we released, why we think it’s valuable, and what comes next for Napster as the end of the year approaches.

First, a look at what launched this week.

### Napster Pulse

When Napster Chief Technology Officer Edo Segal was managing about 100 engineers, he ran into an obvious, seemingly unsolvable roadblock. He wanted to get individual status updates from everyone, so nothing slipped past him, but couldn’t have an actual check-in with each engineer each week; there just weren’t enough hours in the day.

Instead, he used AI to build a digital twin of himself and a platform where it could have conversations with those engineers. In the interview with the Twin, employees could ask questions and get answers in real time, without having to wait for a meeting that might be impossible to schedule. While this ended up being the solution our own employees needed, even we were skeptical at first.

We asked, “Who wants to be interviewed by an AI?”. It turns out, in our internal testing, people preferred this type of interaction.

The reason why comes down to flexibility, convenience, and quick results.

When a manager or HR representative sends out a survey gauging employee satisfaction, they receive a series of ticked boxes and half-hearted open-ended responses in return. Without a real conversation, employers lose the ability to ask follow-ups, infer meaning, and get limited information about what their direct reports or employees actually want.

But a conversation on a person’s own timetable and their own terms with a digital twin provides real, helpful context in a less stressful environment. People freeze up when they are put on the spot to provide critical feedback for their boss; the stakes are lower when the listener is synthetic. We call this product Pulse because it provides that crucial touch-point interview that’s needed to keep team relationships flowing and productive.

Agents run the conversations, and instead of providing a manager with 500 verbatim transcripts, it pulls out the most relevant parts to form a short summary. From there, the manager can address the team’s pressing concerns and schedule person-to-person follow-ups to fix anything that’s really broken.

Those dynamic human-to-human conversations should still happen, but our people-management tool provides the bridge until those one-on-one conversations can happen. It’s a product we needed and one we believe other companies will need in order to understand a dynamic workforce that no current solutions can keep up with.

### The Enterprise Plan on the Napster App

Another product we shared this week allows everyone in a company to get the kind of support executives have relied on for decades.

The Enterprise Plan for the Napster App, launched on desktop Tuesday, gives every employee a crew: a team of specialized agents that do work for you rather than one do-everything assistant. That’s how people already get good work done. You don’t rely on one superhuman; you bring together a team of experts. We launched the Sales and Life Crews alongside the new app experience after some promising internal testing, and we can’t wait to see what our partners can do when each of their people has a team backing them up.

These agents are coworkers, not simply assistants. Each one has its own computer in the cloud and sees a task through to the end. An assistant suggests; a coworker does.

Several companies have launched do-it-all personal agents in recent months, but we went with the Crew approach, even though it took more time and attention. Feedback from Napster’s own salespeople and staff, who put the product to use for more than a month, told us it would be worth the wait.

Our own sales team ran the Sales Crew on their actual accounts, and the biggest difference came from what the company taught the crew: our products, our pricing, our discount rules. Onboarding a crew, it turns out, looks a lot like onboarding a new hire: You info-dump, keep an eye on early results, correct mistakes, and reward good work. And like a new hire, our agents got more valuable the more they learned about how Napster’s business works.

The future of the workplace is one in which we will be working in tandem with AI. As we create our coworkers, we have to learn how to be good colleagues to them, too. You don’t get that insight from polishing a demo. You gather it from giving smart people the product and listening to their advice, even if it temporarily slows you down.

We’re live at Microsoft Ignite talking about this new kind of working relationship, with both Pulse and the app available to try out. Find us at Booth 1754 (R) for demos.

cross_cutting.title: We let an AI agent help run our Product Hunt launch. Here's what happened.
cross_cutting.description: On Nov 17 we launched Appxiom on Product Hunt. ... Appxiom detects crashes, freezes, memory leaks, failed network calls and broken user journeys in mobile and web apps. ... Our tagline went through several rewrites before we landed on "Context layer for AI coding agents to detect ... all claimed more than the product does.
cross_cutting.content:
## DEV Community

On Nov 17 we launched Appxiom on Product Hunt. It turned out to be the second-busiest day in Product Hunt's history: 1,604 launches, 43 of them featured.

We finished #4 Product of the Day with 289 upvotes and 45 comments. In the two days after launch, 9 new users signed up.

We're a small, bootstrapped team. Here's how we ran the launch, and what we'd do differently.

## What Appxiom does

Coding agents can read your entire repo. They can't see what breaks once your app is in people's hands.

Appxiom detects crashes, freezes, memory leaks, failed network calls and broken user journeys in mobile and web apps. It exposes that context to your coding agent through an MCP server and Skills, so an agent like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex can pull up issues, occurrences and their impact on user goals with tools such asget_gfi_issues and get_issue_occurrence_details.

One rule we held onto all through the launch: Appxiom supplies the context. Your agent and your developers decide the root cause and the fix. We never claim Appxiom fixes bugs on its own, because it doesn't.

SDKs today: Android, iOS, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform and Web (any JS/TS framework, with extra React support). React Native and Shopify are coming soon.

## How the agent helped run the launch

We worked with Claude through the whole launch. Roughly, the split looked like this.

What the agent did:

- Planned the launch and kept a single plan doc up to date as decisions changed
- Drafted and stress-tested the tagline, description and maker comment
- Built the Product Hunt landing page and badge embed on our website, and prepared the launch post for our blog
- Drafted outreach messages
- Checked claims against our docs before they went into any copy
- Pulled together a post-launch report from Product Hunt, analytics and email data (that's where the numbers above come from)

What we kept:

- Every final call: positioning, launch date, what we'd claim and what we wouldn't
- The gallery images and demo video (Andrea on our team made those)
- Part of the outreach, and the conversations with people in the comments

The agent did the legwork, and we made the calls. That's the same split Appxiom is built around: the tool gives the agent context, and a human stays in charge of decisions.

## What we learned

### 1. Get the one line right before anything else

Our tagline went through several rewrites before we landed on "Context layer for AI coding agents to detect & fix bugs." The tempting versions all claimed more than the product does. Once we had a line that was both accurate and clear, the description, gallery and maker comment came together much faster.

Having an agent helped here. Every new draft got checked against a positioning rule we'd written down, so claims didn't creep back in.

### 2. The first few hours decide the ranking

We climbed steadily all day, but the top 3 pulled ahead early and the gap never closed. They also had far more comments than we did.

If we launched again, we'd put much more effort into starting real conversations in the first hours, not just later in the day.

### 3. Agents are becoming the user

Most of the top products on our launch day, us included, shipped an MCP server.

If you build developer tools, that changes how you design. Your docs, tool names and response fields are now an interface that an agent reads. Clear, predictable tools matter as much as a clean dashboard does.

### 4. Lead with the business problem, not the feature list

The example we kept coming back to: developers will often fix a crash on a settings screen almost nobody visits before an API delay in the signup flow. The crash looks worse. The signup delay costs more, because fewer people finish signing up.

That's why we built Goal Friction Impact (GFI). You mark a user goal (signup, checkout, anything) with two SDK calls. Appxiom tracks how many people start and finish it, where they drop off, and which bug was in the way. Your agent can then work on the issue that costs you the most completed goals, not the one with the highest crash count.

On our demo dashboard, launch-day visitors spent the most time on exactly those goal screens.

### 5. Pick your launch date around your team

Launch on a day when the people who can answer technical questions are free to reply to comments all day. Moving a launch by a week is cheap. A launch day with nobody around to answer questions isn't.

## Try it

Appxiom has a 30-day free trial. Your coding agent can do the setup: add the Skills, then the SDK.

Thanks to our team, Don, Andrea, Nikhil, Sandra and Jefin, and to everyone who upvoted, commented and tried it.

## Want to make DEV your full-time job?

We're hiring a full-time Community Manager to look after DEV every day: reading, posting, moderating, and helping members get fast, thoughtful answers.

## Top comments (1)

Subscribe

Interesting that 289 upvotes and 45 comments turned into 9 signups in two days. Looking back, do you think the traffic was mostly other makers and upvoters rather than people with the actual problem? And what would you change first to start those conversations early in the day?

cross_cutting.content:

# Product launch checklist for AI products: what has to work first

## Before a product launch, an email assistant can be ready to draft a reply while the store owner still decides whether to send it.

Suppose your next product launch is two weeks away. You’ve built an assistant that drafts replies for small online stores. A shopper writes, “Where’s my order? If it hasn’t shipped, I’d like a refund.” Your demo tested order updates and refund requests separately. What should the assistant do when they arrive in the same email?

For this launch, the store owner reviews every draft, and auto-send stays off. Messages that need a refund decision go straight to the owner. To decide whether the drafting feature is ready, test it on the store’s own inbox and record which replies the owner sends, edits, or writes again from scratch.

## What should you check before an AI product launch?

Check that the core task works on inputs you did not choose, that the product knows what it must not do, and that you can trace every output and switch sending off.

1. Test on real customer inputs. Ask a few pilot stores for a week of their actual customer emails, with their permission, instead of reusing the demo set.

2. Define one task and one pass criterion. For the email assistant: a draft the store owner sends unchanged or with wording edits only.

3. List what the product must not do, and test those cases on purpose. Promising a refund, changing an order, or giving legal advice are examples.

4. Check the failure path. Decide what the user sees when the model times out, returns nothing, or is unsure.

5. Make every output traceable. Keep the input, the prompt version, the model, the output, and what the user did with it.

6. Check that you can disable sending and restore the previous prompt. Once a reply reaches a customer, the owner needs a way to follow up.

7. Know the cost per task at the usage you expect. A price you cannot explain per task is hard to defend later.

A demo inbox with separate examples for order updates and refunds won’t tell you what the assistant does when a shopper asks for both.

## What counts as usable?

Usable means the user finishes the task with the output instead of redoing it, measured on their own inputs. Accuracy on your test set is a different measure.

Count a draft as usable if the owner sends it unchanged or edits only the wording. If the owner has to correct an order status, remove a refund promise, or write the reply from scratch, count that email as a miss.

## Get BG Yoo’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

Count every email in the drafting scope, including timeouts and empty responses. Emails meant for the owner, such as refund decisions, are counted separately: check that the owner received the original message and can see why it was handed over.

Set the bar before the pilot starts. If you decide what counts as good after seeing the results, the bar tends to move to wherever the results landed.

## What should you not launch with?

Do not launch with anything that can make a promise, move money, or act for the user without review, and do not launch with anything you cannot observe.

• Anything that acts for the user without review.

• Answers outside the scope you tested.

• Data sources you have not checked.

• A price you cannot explain per task.

• Claims your evidence does not support, such as accuracy rates or time saved you have not measured on real use.

Drafts appear in a review inbox, and nothing reaches a shopper until the owner sends it. An email that asks for a refund arrives without a draft, with the original message and a one-line reason for the handover. If the assistant times out, the email is marked as having no draft instead of showing an empty reply.

## How do you handle what isn’t ready?

Turn it off, tell users plainly, and keep a list of what is not ready, with the condition that would let each item ship.

## How we think about this at CUBIG

When a second store joins the pilot, rerun the mixed order-and-refund email against that store’s policy. The first pilot tells you how the assistant handled the first store’s rules.

We use Syntitan, our platform, to generate test cases from an SOP. In an internal comparison using five sample SOPs and the same agent settings, a separate LLM judge classified 67 of 80 Syntitan cases as going beyond the obvious scenarios, compared with 23 of 80 from single-pass generation.

For the email assistant, one case worth keeping is the shopper who asks about an order and a refund in the same message. Before launch, put that email through the product and check the owner’s inbox. Did the original message arrive? Can the owner see why it was handed over? Did anything go out to the shopper?

# Argentum AI signs USD $630 million Kyndryl data deal
Thu, 19th Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Argentum AI has signed a USD $630 million data centre agreement with Kyndryl, covering 20 years and an initial 10 megawatts of capacity.

The site will host NVIDIA B300 systems for AI inference, with deployment already under way in a Tier III facility, the companies said.

The deal brings together a GPU cloud provider that finances and operates its own clusters and an IT infrastructure services group that runs large-scale technology environments for customers in more than 60 countries.

Argentum said the arrangement gives it access to a facility built for the power density required by current-generation GPU systems and is intended to give customers faster access to inference capacity.

Under the collaboration, Kyndryl will provide facility capacity and data centre operations. Argentum said it is deploying the systems as part of its effort to serve AI model builders, inference providers and enterprise customers that rent dedicated bare-metal GPU capacity.

Inference focus

The agreement centres on AI inference rather than model training, reflecting a growing area of the AI infrastructure market as companies seek to run production workloads at scale.

Argentum described itself as the flagship anchor tenant at the facility. It said its technology supports widely used AI applications, but did not identify specific customers in the announcement.

The companies also said they intend to expand their work together as Argentum grows. They did not disclose additional financial terms or expansion targets.

For Argentum, the arrangement secures a long-term base for GPU deployment at a time when access to suitable data centre space and power remains constrained in many markets. Facilities able to support dense GPU installations have become a key bottleneck for companies expanding AI services.

For Kyndryl, the deal adds a named AI infrastructure tenant to its data centre operations business and gives it a role in a market segment tied to demand for inference computing.

"Partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for Argentum AI," said Andrew Sobko, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Argentum AI.

"This agreement reflects our shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale."

Kyndryl described the arrangement as a new use for its available capacity and operational experience in mission-critical environments.

"Our agreement gives us a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way. Coupled with our mission-critical capabilities and decades of operational and services experience, it will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers," said Jamie Rutledge, President of Kyndryl U.S.

Argentum originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, then supplies dedicated infrastructure to customers that need direct access to graphics processing units for AI workloads. Kyndryl, which was spun out of IBM, focuses on designing, building, managing and modernising large information systems for enterprise and public sector users.

The collaboration underlines how specialist GPU cloud providers are turning to long-term infrastructure agreements to secure power and floor space as demand for AI inference grows.

cross_cutting.content:
# US Government backs WinDC's AI factory rollout in Australia

By Dylan Bushell-Embling

Thursday, 19 November, 2026

Australian modular data centre infrastructure developer WinDC has partnered with edge infrastructure company Armada with the goal of building up to 3 GW of AI computing capacity across Australia and New Zealand by the end of 2030.

The US Government-backed build-out could be worth up to US$30 billion (AU$44.61 billion) in total project investment. The rollout will begin with an initial 11 MW deployment across five Australian states, followed by a further 230 MW build-out in 2027. The total deployment could span 40 sites by 2030.

WinDC is part of the Australian rollout supporting the US Government’s push to accelerate the global deployment of US AI technology, with Armada having been named a Priority Team Leader under the American SI (Super Intelligence) Exports Program.

The American sovereign AI stack led by Armada consists of a consortium combining Armada’s modular data centres with Dell computing and storage and Microsoft’s Azure Local and Foundry Local platforms. The program provides designated consortia with access to federal financing agencies, US Government advocacy and prioritised export licence processing. WinDC and Armada intend to explore potential financing support for future deployments, including through the Export-Import Bank of the United States.

WinDC CEO Andrew Sjoquist said with the deal, the US Government is backing the world’s most advanced AI technology to be built in Australia.

“That puts us at the front of the queue at a time when every nation on Earth is competing for computing capacity,” he said. “Our immediate focus is delivering 230 MW of new capacity in 2027, while building towards a national network that could attract more than US$30 billion in investment by the end of the decade. This is an opportunity to bring substantial investment into regional Australia, create economic activity around energy generation sites and turn Australian energy into computing capacity that can be sold to customers around the world.”

WinDC’s business model involves deploying factory-built modular AI data centres at or near existing energy generation sites, including renewable sites such as wind and solar plants. Building compute capacity close to available electricity promises to address issues such as grid constraints and lengthy construction timelines associated with metropolitan data centre precincts. WinDC is targeting deployment timelines of around 90 days where sites, power and approvals are ready. The play also presents an opportunity to make use of the renewable energy that would otherwise be curtailed, with an estimated 7 TWh of wind and solar generation curtailed across Australia’s electricity market in 2025.

Armada’s Leviathan modular data centres provide up to 2 MW of computing infrastructure per unit with multiple facilities capable of being connected to operate as a single distributed computing network.

“Our approach allows us to deploy capacity quickly, expand as demand grows and build a national network capable of supporting both Australian businesses and international customers,” Sjoquist said.

He added that the project could establish Australia as a major exporter of AI computing services, particularly to markets across the Indo-Pacific using the subsea cable infrastructure connecting Western Australia to the region. In Southeast Asia alone there would be an addressable market of at least 500 million people within around 50 ms of latency.

“For decades, Australia has shipped its energy overseas as raw resources. Now we can use that energy here, turn it into intelligence and sell it to the world, with Western Australia as the gateway to some of the fastest-growing AI markets on the planet,” he said.

The deal follows the Trump administration’s announcement of a US$85 million (AU$126.4 million) agreement between Quad countries the US, India, Australia and Japan to expand access to trusted AI ecosystems across the Indo-Pacific region, as well as plans to launch an AI accelerator.

# Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Sakura Internet sign MoU to establish sovereign AI infrastructure in Japan

Will form a strategic alliance to develop modular AI data centers

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) and cloud provider and data center operator Sakura Internet have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish sovereign AI and cloud infrastructure in Japan.

Under the MoU, the two will develop modular AI data centers that can be built efficiently and quickly, and look for opportunities to strengthen digital infrastructure in the country for sovereign AI workloads.

"As AI becomes national infrastructure, that infrastructure has to be resilient in both how it is built and how it is operated. With Sakura Internet, we want to give Japan a sovereign AI foundation that is secure, available when it matters, and fast enough to keep pace with demand. This is part of the MHI ITO(Note2) initiative: combining our strengths with the right partner to deliver value to far more customers," said Masayuki Suematsu, executive vice president and chief strategy officer, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.

Kunihiro Tanaka, founder, CEO, and president, Sakura Internet, added: "With the rapid spread of AI, digital infrastructure such as cloud and data centers has become essential to society and industry. In this collaboration, we will combine MHI's technology and expertise in social infrastructure with our own experience building and operating cloud and data centers. Together, we aim to create new options for the domestic digital infrastructure that the sovereign AI and sovereign cloud era requires."

Earlier this year, MHI said that it was planning to revamp its gas turbine production process to drive output and cut manufacturing time to meet demand from the AI data center sector. The company launched an on-prem containerized data center offering in February.

Sakura Internet was selected by Japan's Digital Agency as a Government Cloud service provider for fiscal year 2026. It operates data centers in Tokyo, Osaka, and Hokkaido. Earlier this year, the company formed a consortium with NTT and Tokyu Land with plans to establish a data center cluster in Ishikari City in Hokkaido. Sakura Internet has operated its data center in Ishikari since 2011, and has recently been expanding and deploying GPUs at the site.

cross_cutting.content:
# Partnership brings sovereign AI infrastructure to Europe

### Dublin, Ireland

Armada, the Sovereign SI Infrastructure company, and Johnson Controls have partnered to start production at Galleon Forge Two, Armada’s first European manufacturing operation, located within a Johnson Controls facility in Dublin. It is the second Galleon Forge established at a Johnson Controls facility, following Galleon Forge One in Gilbert, Arizona, USA.

Together, the two sites expand Armada's manufacturing footprint and mark the start of continuous production of sovereign computing infrastructure in Europe. The companies marked the milestone with the completion of the first Dublin-built Leviathan, a multi-megawatt-scale modular data centre headed to Fossefall in Norway. Europe's first Leviathan was engineered, integrated, and tested entirely at Galleon Forge Two — proof that sovereign AI infrastructure for Europe can now be built in Europe.

Leviathan combines Armada's sovereign computing infrastructure and software with Johnson Controls differentiated thermal management technology and industrial-scale manufacturing capabilities. The Johnson Controls thermal portfolio spans the end-to-end thermal chain, including coolant distribution units, chillers, and building controls, and supports high-density compute with zero-water cooling technologies designed to reduce energy use and noise.

#### A manufacturing model built to expand

Galleon Forge Two follows Galleon Forge One at the Johnson Controls manufacturing site in Gilbert, Arizona, where continuous production is expected to begin in early 2027 across up to 400,000 square feet, supporting more than 500 jobs with additional roles across the domestic supply chain. Further manufacturing expansion is planned at a Johnson Controls site in Edmonton, Canada. The Galleon Forge model is designed to be anchored by any nation or region that wants sovereign AI infrastructure built at home, with local jobs, a local supply chain, and capacity that stays under local control.

Galleon Forge Two is located at a Johnson Controls manufacturing site in Dublin, Ireland, spanning 90,000 square feet and is supported by approximately 700 Johnson Controls engineers, technicians and other skilled workers, with additional roles across the European supply chain. For European governments and enterprises, the implications go beyond capacity: the infrastructure supporting their AI no longer has to be imported or rented. It is manufactured in Europe, owned by customers, and operated on their terms.

"The speed of the sovereign AI revolution requires a new approach to meet demand,” said Dan Wright, Co-founder and CEO of Armada. "The Galleon Forge model keeps producing, and it’s designed to keep expanding. We can now deliver to any nation or organisation that needs advanced computing infrastructure manufactured within its own borders — owned and controlled on its own terms."

“We’ve been building modular infrastructure for nearly two decades. What’s different today is the scale, density and speed AI demands,” said Austin Domenici, President, Global Data Center Solutions, Johnson Controls. “With Armada, we’re combining that experience with our thermal expertise and manufacturing scale to complete more of the complex integration work in the factory and bring compute online faster and more predictably.”

Leviathan runs on the Armada Platform, which manages power, cooling, and compute across every unit and runs the latest open-source or proprietary models. Customers own the infrastructure and control every layer, with no dependence on an external cloud. As part of the Armada Sovereign SI Grid, Leviathans run as one fleet, so critical workloads never depend on a single site.

#### Early deployments in Norway and Australia

Fossefall has placed an initial order for five Leviathan modular data centres totaling more than 9 MW, beginning with the unit completed today, with delivery of all five scheduled by the first quarter of 2027. Finding partners in Europe was particularly important for their vision of sovereignty.

"Europe needs more advanced computing infrastructure, and the focus now needs to be on getting projects built,” said Øyvind L. Vesterdal, CEO of Fossefall. “Working with Armada and Johnson Controls gives us a more standardised and modular approach to deployment. This can help shorten timelines and make projects easier to develop in close cooperation with local communities. With access to clean energy, political stability and a suitable climate, the Nordics are well positioned for large-scale AI infrastructure.”

In Australia, Win DC plans to deploy 11 MW of modular data centre capacity across renewable-energy sites, placing compute near wind, solar, and battery generation.

"Australia's energy transition depends on building AI infrastructure in the right place, where the renewable energy is, rather than waiting for a grid that can't scale fast enough to carry it," said Andrew Sjoquist, Founder and CEO of Win DC. "Leviathan lets us bring compute directly to clean power and scale it with the workload."

# Deutsche Telekom : advances sovereign AI in Germany

Published on 11/19/2026 at 01:33 pm IST

Publicnow

T.Capital Tech Fund has invested 100 million euros in Mistral's Series D funding round. As Deutsche Telekom's strategic investment arm, T.Capital manages over 2 billion euros in assets on behalf of the Group and invests in companies that support its strategic priorities.

The investment marks a first step towards combining Deutsche Telekom's sovereign infrastructure, customer relationships and integration expertise with Mistral's frontier models, enterprise software and deployment capabilities as part of a future strategic partnership. Together, the companies plan to support German businesses and public institutions adopt AI tailored to their needs, particularly in industrial and regulated sectors.

The collaboration builds on Deutsche Telekom's investments in sovereign AI infrastructure in Germany and Mistral's growing presence in the country, including its recently established Munich hub.

Both companies are committed to supporting a competitive and sovereign European AI ecosystem, spanning AI infrastructure, models and enterprise applications.

Ferri Abolhassan, member of the Board of Management of Deutsche Telekom AG and CEO of T-Systems International GmbH, said: "Europe's competitiveness depends on our ability to develop and use powerful AI. Businesses must be able to trust this technology while retaining control over their data. Our Industrial AI Cloud provides a strong foundation for sovereign AI in Germany. With the investment in Mistral, we are expanding the combination of frontier European AI technology and engineering expertise with trusted infrastructure and integration capabilities to help businesses across Germany put trusted AI to work."

Johan Bergqvist, Chief Financial Officer, said: "Germany is known as the industrial backbone of Europe, and AI is now core to industrial competitiveness. We built Mistral so that European enterprises can deploy frontier AI they fully control, on their own data, in their own infrastructure. T.Capital's investment is a strong signal: together, DT and Mistral can bring sovereign, trustworthy AI to German industry and public institutions at scale."

Maneesh Sharma, Partner at T.Capital Tech Fund said: "Mistral has established itself as one of Europe's leading AI companies, combining world-class technology with a strong focus on enterprise needs. We see significant potential for Mistral to become a global leader in enterprise AI. Our 100 million euros investment reflects our conviction in the team, technology and market, while creating exciting opportunities with Deutsche Telekom."
